entries.section: (1) The captivity of Tobit

paragraphs.text: Exile: captivity.
All that he could obtain: all that he gained of money, or food and drink.
Tobit: a Hebrew word meaning God is good, or the blessed one.
Nephthali: a Hebrew word meaning wrestlings.
Nahshon: a Hebrew word meaning a serpent.

Nephthali is the son of Jacob and one of the tribes of the children of Israel. His tribe settled in the north of Palestine from the days of Joshua, when the land was divided, in a region called Galilee, that is, Galilee of the Gentiles, where they were close to the Gentiles and mixed with them. As for Nahshon, he is the son of Amminadab, one of the leaders of the tribe of Judah (see Map 1, p. 265). In the spiritual and symbolic interpretation, Tobit engaged in wrestlings in the midst of the Gentiles, and he triumphed over Satan, the old serpent, and stood firm in faith and holy living despite all afflictions. That is, the man who is blessed by God is the one who strives in his life against Satan, wrestles, and overcomes by the power of God, confident that God helps him and puts the devil under his feet, just as the city of Nahshon was beneath the city of Nephthali, in which Tobit lived.

entries.section: (1) The captivity of Tobit

paragraphs.text: The captivity of the northern kingdom, which is the kingdom of Israel whose capital was Samaria, took place in several stages. The second stage was at the hand of Shalmaneser, who is mentioned here, who reigned during the period (728-722 BC). He took many of the Jews captive and besieged Samaria but did not capture it; rather, King Sargon, his successor, captured it. The kingdom of Assyria lies north of the River Tigris, that is, in present-day Iraq, and its dominion extended until it took the whole region of the Levant and a large part of Judea, as far as the borders of Egypt (see Map 2, p. 265). Here the Holy Bible bears witness to Tobit that he was a man who held fast to the Law of God and His ordinances, not only among his people in Judea, but also after his captivity and his transfer to the land of Assyria.

entries.section: (1) The captivity of Tobit

paragraphs.text: For he used to share all that he obtained with his brethren, the captives who were of his own race.

The holiness of a man is not shown only in easy circumstances, but also in exile and in adverse circumstances. Do you hold fast to God even though those around you are preoccupied with things other than the religious life?

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: The Holy Bible tells us here about the early life of Tobit in his youth, when he was in Palestine in the city of Nephthali. He was a young man of tender age, able to work more than others, not in order to become rich and enjoy the pleasures of the world, but to help the poor and the needy. He did not act with the recklessness of youth, but with the maturity of men.

From the longer text of this book we understand that Tobit was an orphan and that his devout grandmother Deborah raised him; she took care to teach him the faith and the ritual practices, and he held fast to them when he grew up.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: As for doctrine, Tobit held fast to his faith. He would worship only in the temple of God in Jerusalem, although it was a long distance from him, and he did not go to worship at the images made by Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who divided the kingdom in the days of Rehoboam the son of King Solomon. Jeroboam made two calves and set them in the two cities of Bethel and Dan, so that the Jews of the northern kingdom, which comprises ten tribes, would worship them. In this way he ensured that they would not go to Jerusalem and consequently would not be subject to the king of Judah who lived in Jerusalem. By this act of Jeroboam the Jews were made to worship idols, but a few remained who held fast to the faith and worshiped none but God in the temple of Jerusalem; among them was this Tobit, great in his faith.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: Firstfruits: that is, the first-born produce, the first thing a man obtains from the produce of the fields or the vineyards, or the like. Tithes: that is, the tenths, as the Law commanded that they be given to God.
Tobit was diligent in offering the firstfruits and the tithes, keeping the law of the Lord and His ordinances, and caring to show hospitality to strangers.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: Tobit used to direct his tithes in the third year to the care of strangers.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: His youth: his boyhood and his young manhood.
According to: in keeping with.
He was meticulous in keeping up all the works of goodness and the worship of the Lord that he had kept previously.

How beautiful it is for you to have a distinguished character in giving and not in taking, so that you think how to labor in order to give rest to others. Do not think of your own pleasure and personal mood, especially in the years of youth, when a person has the strength and vitality to accomplish many services. And hold fast to God even if others oppose you and differ from you.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: Anna: a Hebrew name meaning tenderness, or grace.

When Tobit grew up and became a man, he chose a Jewish wife of his own tribe, whose name was Anna, because he held fast to the Law of God, and he begot a son by her, whom he named Tobias after his own name.
For the one truly blessed by God has the tenderness and grace of God poured out upon him, and his fruit also becomes blessed.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: Here, too, a new quality appears in Tobit, as a father and educator, who cares to bring up his son in a religious upbringing, in the fear of God and in keeping away from evils.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: Around the year 725 BC, Tobit was taken captive with his kindred from the city of Nephthali. King Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, carried him away to the city of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, which lies on the River Tigris; after it was destroyed, the city of Mosul in Iraq now stands in its place (see Map 2, p. 265). Such was the policy of the kings of Assyria: to abolish the nationhood of those whom they conquered, so they removed them from their countries to other lands in the empire and brought others to take their place. Thus Tobit suddenly found himself living among the Gentiles, he and his kindred.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's piety in his youth

paragraphs.text: In this foreign land the Jews were influenced by the Gentiles around them; they began to eat their foods and to imitate their customs. But Tobit remained firm in his faith, eating only the permitted foods stipulated by the Law of Moses, and refusing any food God had forbidden even if the Gentiles around him ate it.

entries.section: (3) His favor with the king

paragraphs.text: Favor: grace.
Here we see God's blessings upon His devout ones. Because Tobit held fast to the Law of God, God gave him grace in the eyes of King Shalmaneser, who lived with him in the capital Nineveh.

entries.section: (3) His favor with the king

paragraphs.text: Tobit came to work for the king, as appears in the Hebrew text of this book, as a purveyor, that is, as a contractor supplying the needs of the royal palace. So he acquired wealth from his work and became one of the king's close associates. The king granted him special privileges, permission to travel between all the countries of the empire as he wished, and freedom to do as he pleased, because he was one of the king's own; and he gave him silver and many material gifts.

entries.section: (3) His favor with the king

paragraphs.text: Tobit used these privileges to travel to the various lands in order to visit the Jews and guide them to the commandments and laws of God, to confirm them in the faith, and to advise them not to mingle with the customs and sins of the Gentiles.

Do you use the blessings that God gives you for your personal enjoyment, or for the service of those around you? Do you think of yourself and your desires, or do you feel your responsibility for others and strive for their comfort and for binding them to the Church?

entries.section: (3) His favor with the king

paragraphs.text: Rages: it lies eight kilometers southeast of Tehran, in present-day Iran, beside the Caspian Sea, and it was eleven days' journey from Ecbatana or Hamadan. It is said to be the birthplace of Zoroaster, and it later became the religious center of the Magi (see Map 2, p. 265). Media: an ancient and powerful country, whose place is now Iran. It was bounded on the northeast by the Caspian Sea, on the east by the desert of Persia, on the south by Persia, and on the west by Assyria and Armenia. Its length from north to south is about one thousand kilometers, and from east to west about four hundred kilometers. It was later united with the kingdom of Persia and defeated the kingdom of Babylon and dominated the whole world. The Medes, the inhabitants of Media, are descended from Madai the son of Japheth (Gen 10:2). Favored him with it: bestowed it on him and gave it to him specially.

While Tobit was visiting his brethren, he came to the city of Rages, which is in the kingdom of Media. Tobit began to visit his Jewish brethren and ask about them, to care for the poor and needy among them. He had with him some of the gifts the king had given him, ten talents of silver. A talent of silver equals three thousand shekels, * that is, about one thousand five hundred American dollars at today's price.

entries.section: (3) His favor with the king

paragraphs.text: Want: poverty.
The talent: the weight (talent).

Tobit found one of the Jews in financial distress, so he gave him the silver he had with him as a loan. This Jew, whose name was Gabael, wrote a bond in his own name, that is, an authenticated document, declaring that he had borrowed this sum from Tobit and was bound to return it to him; it served as a receipt for the borrowed sum.

Here Tobit is a type of Christ, who goes about everywhere doing good and proclaims liberty to the captives, as Isaiah prophesied. The silver is a symbol of the righteousness of man. Christ, the Son of Man, has given us His righteousness, and we are justified by it. Gabael, a stranger in this world, received righteousness from Tobit, who is a type of Christ, so the problem of his need and his poverty in righteousness was solved by the righteousness he received. The writing of the bond here means that man (Gabael) had become indebted for the amount of the debt to divine justice, which Christ paid on our behalf.

entries.section: (4) Sennacherib's persecution of the Jews

paragraphs.text: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, had taken captive a considerable number of Jews and besieged Samaria for three years, but he died in the year 722 BC and was succeeded by King Sargon, who captured Samaria and took another number of Jews captive. Tobit kept his position and his privileges throughout the reign of these two kings. The Holy Bible does not mention King Sargon, for the sake of brevity in the historical events, since they are not the aim of the Holy Bible. Then in the year 705 BC, King Sennacherib reigned, who hated the Jews, and tried to take possession of the southern kingdom of the Jews, that is, the kingdom of Judah, whose capital was Jerusalem. He besieged it, and the Rabshakeh, the commander of his army, stood and reviled the Jews (2 Kgs 18:19) and mocked their God, and sent letters from King Sennacherib full of threats and reproach to Hezekiah king of Judah. Hezekiah prayed and sought help from Isaiah the prophet, who reassured him that God would deliver His people. That very night God sent His angel, who killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand of Sennacherib's soldiers, and the rest fled in shame to Sennacherib.

entries.section: (5) The deliverance of Tobit from the hand of Sennacherib

paragraphs.text: King Sennacherib heard of what Tobit was doing in helping his persecuted Jewish brethren, and he was enraged at him and issued an order to kill him and seize all his property.

entries.section: (5) The deliverance of Tobit from the hand of Sennacherib

paragraphs.text: So Tobit fled at once, with his wife Anna and his son Tobias, leaving behind all his possessions, and hid with one of his Jewish friends. Because he had so many who loved him, no one informed against him; rather, they took care to host and hide him. Sennacherib is a type of the devil, who is enraged at the power of God, who protects His people, and who tries to devour us. But God, even though He sometimes allows affliction, does so within limits, and does not allow Satan to rule over us, and with the temptation makes a way of escape, as He made the love of the Jews, their hospitality and their hiding of Tobit and his family, a cause of their salvation. Tobit's love for works of mercy also appears, especially in afflictions: he is courageous and trusts in God, doing the work of God and sacrificing himself; therefore God preserved him, and King Sennacherib did not harm him.

entries.section: (5) The deliverance of Tobit from the hand of Sennacherib

paragraphs.text: Then we see God's vengeance on the wicked in order to deliver His children. After the defeat of Sennacherib's army, which had besieged Jerusalem, and the resulting rage of King Sennacherib and his killing of many of the Jews, he went in to worship in the temple of idols, of a god called Nisroch, and his two sons attacked him and killed him with the sword.

entries.section: (5) The deliverance of Tobit from the hand of Sennacherib

paragraphs.text: Another son of his reigned in his place, called King Esarhaddon (2 Kgs 19:37). This was in the year 681 BC. He did not hate the Jews, so he restored all his money to Tobit, and Tobit came out of hiding and returned to his house.

Tobit's return to his first position was helped by the fact that his nephew Ahikar (as the longer text of this book mentions) held the position of chief cupbearer, keeper of the signet, and master of administration and accounts. This was by the providence of God, so Tobit regained all his former standing.
Thus the promise of God is fulfilled, who fights for His children while they hold their peace, so that the heart of everyone who does good and fears God may be at ease.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: It is clear from Tobit's conduct that he held fast to the Law and to the feasts of the Lord, despite being in captivity among the Gentiles, far from Jerusalem. He used these occasions to hold love feasts that bound the people of God in exile to one another and encouraged them in the midst of afflictions, besides being an opportunity to invite the poor and needy.

This feast was the feast of Pentecost (as the longer text of this book mentions), which is the Feast of Weeks, in which the Law calls for care for the poor, the strangers and the needy (Deut 16:11, 12). So Tobit was especially attentive to this feast and made a great dinner, to which he invited his Jewish brethren, especially the poor.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: He asked his son to invite those of his tribe who feared God, to share with him in this feast. For this reason the Church in the New Testament takes care to hold the holy feasts, in which the faithful gather around the table of the Lord, that is, His holy altar, and partake of His most holy Body and Blood. This encourages them during their exile in this world, and it is also an opportunity to care for the poor and needy, that they may rejoice with all the faithful.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: The younger Tobias is also seen following his father's example in works of mercy. While he was inviting the devout Jews who care for the feasts of the Lord to come to the dinner, he noticed in the marketplace one of the Jews lying on the ground, strangled, one of those reached by the hand of the persecuting ruler. He hurried to tell his father Tobit what he had seen, and the father left the dinner without eating, in order to do the work of mercy first.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: So Tobit hurried and quietly carried the body and hid it in his house until night should come, when he could bury it away from the eyes of the ruler's soldiers, who wanted to torment the Jews. Here Tobit's love for works of mercy appears, before his own rest, his joys, and the food he needed.

The longer text mentions Tobit's adherence to the Law: he washed after the day had passed, and so he was purified and was able to eat of the dinner. He was meticulous in applying the Law in the hardest circumstances, for the Law provides that whoever is defiled by touching a dead body remains unclean until evening, then washes and becomes clean, and may then eat and touch everything (Lev 22:6).

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: Here, too, the fear of God appears in Tobit's heart, for he felt that God's permitting the killing of the children of his people was because of their many sins and their distance from God. So his heart was humble, fearing God, mixed with feelings of love and sympathy over the death of loved ones, sharing the sorrows of the martyr's family. Tobit bore a heart full of love for God and for others.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: In addition, Tobit was aware and a student of the Holy Scriptures, and was influenced by them. He remembered the sayings of the prophets, among them Amos (Amos 8:10), who warned and cautioned, by the decree of the Lord, that the feasts would be turned into mourning and weeping, so that people might return to God in repentance. The prophet Amos preceded Tobit by about one hundred and fifty years.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: Under the cover of the night and its darkness, Tobit was able to bury the body of the martyr, away from the eyes of the ruler's soldiers.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: Those gathered at the dinner in his house, and all his relatives, were astonished at his continuing in works of mercy and burying the dead, because for this very reason King Sennacherib had earlier ordered him to be killed, and Tobit had fled and God had saved him, as we mentioned. They rebuked him and warned him against burying the dead and helping the needy, because by this he was exposing himself to certain death.

entries.section: (1) Tobit's holding fast to the feasts of the Lord and to works of mercy

paragraphs.text: Here Tobit's faith and fear of God appear: he was not shaken or afraid of their words, but continued in works of mercy. And God preserved him, so the king's hand did not reach him.

If a person's faith in God is strong, he will fear God and take care to carry out His commandments without concern for the words of those around him, and he will even give up his own thinking, trusting in the power of the commandment. And for the sake of his love for God, he is ready to sacrifice his life, and then the grace of God is revealed, which preserves him, and even blesses him and distinguishes him from all around him, as happened with Daniel the prophet, who was thrown into the lions' den because he held fast to prayer to God. God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions and delivered him, and the king raised him to a greater position and put to death those who had accused him.
Beware lest your fear for those around you become a cause of discouraging them and turning them away from the worship and service of God.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: Arrived: came to.

Tobit continued in his care to bury the bodies of the martyrs, despite the great effort it required. One day, after the toil of burying many, when he was fifty-six years old, he returned to his house very tired, and from the extremity of his weariness he fell asleep as soon as he arrived at the house, leaning against a wall outside his house.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: Droppings: the waste (excrement) of a bird.
Swallow: the swallow bird, a kind of bird of the order of the cutters, with a broad beak, slender wings, and a long, ruffled tail.

He was sitting beneath a bird's nest, and the waste (excrement) of this bird fell from the nest while it was hot, and it fell upon his eyes. Perhaps he awoke from his sleep upon this hot substance, which contains acids, or substances very harmful to the eye, and it deprived him of his sight, and he became blind, seeing nothing. It is noted that the waste of this bird is a sticky liquid, which, when it falls on the eye, spreads over it and is quickly absorbed. Its temperature is about forty-two degrees Celsius, and it contains uric acid (Uric acid), which irritates the eyelids, and it also contains ammonia, which causes damage to the cells of the eye and stops the vital processes in it. This waste also contains some salts that damage the retina of the eye. And since there were no quick means of first aid for the eye, it lost the ability to * see.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: The divine inspiration declares God's purpose in this hard trial: that Tobit might be proved and the virtue of patience be shown in him, and that he might be an example to others and a pattern of patience like Job.
There is a similarity between the books of Job and Tobit, in which the following appears:
1- Both were an example of patience.
2- The first chapter in each speaks of his character.
3- The relation of the angels with men appears in both books.
4- The envy of Satan and his opposition to the devout children of God appear in both books, and then their victory over him by the power of God.
5- God's concern for all the prayers and words of men, good and bad, appears clearly in both books.
6- The murmuring of the wife and the friends and their reproach of Job and Tobit.
7- God's declaring His voice clearly at the end of the book, whether by Himself in the case of Job, or through the chief of His angels in the case of Tobit.
8- Both books end with God's blessings upon the one who fears Him, namely Job and Tobit.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: He did not cease: he did not cease.
This indeed happened, for Tobit continued in his piety and in keeping the commandments of God, content with this trial.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: After the trial, too, Tobit remained thankful to God, careful in his conduct in the fear of God.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: His kinsfolk: his relatives.
Tobit's virtues appear in his bearing reproach and his steadfastness in faith, like St. Job, who bore the reproaches of his rich friends, who were kings in their lands.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: Tobit's relatives and friends used to reproach him for his sickness and try to push him to despair of God, who had left him to be afflicted by this trial, and they made him doubt the worth and benefit of all the works of mercy he had done.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: But he rebuked them, that they should not speak such words.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's being struck with blindness and his steadfastness in faith

paragraphs.text: And he declared to them that they are the holy people of God in Him and the children of saints, who live in the hope of eternal life; therefore they do all the virtues and works of mercy and are not concerned with earthly things, whatever trials come upon them, but remain steadfast in their faith.

The longer text mentions that Ahikar, the son of Tobit's brother, who had helped him return to his position after the death of Sennacherib (ch. 1:25), cared for him after he lost his sight, and supported him for two years and attended to his affairs; then he returned to his country where he lived, which was Elymais (Elam). Thus Tobit became in great need of his daily bread.

Be sure that every trial that passes over you, however hard, is by God's permission, for your benefit. And even if the devil, or wicked people, intend evil against you, God will turn the evil into good. The important thing is that you accept the trial with contentment and thanks from the hand of God, and take refuge in God with repentance and prayer, and persevere in the spiritual practices. And be sure also that the trial is necessary for your salvation, so that you may be proved before God and find a great place in Heaven.

entries.section: (3) The reproaches of his wife

paragraphs.text: The weavers: the seamstresses.
Provisions: foods.

Since the righteous Tobit was unable to work, and his nephew Ahikar had left him because he had lost his sight, his wife Anna was forced to work outside her home. This was not customary in that time. Since she knew sewing, she went to a workshop that tailored clothes and worked for them, and what she received as wages she used to buy foods.

entries.section: (3) The reproaches of his wife

paragraphs.text: Anna was able to gather some money, and she bought a kid and brought it to the house.

entries.section: (3) The reproaches of his wife

paragraphs.text: Her husband: her husband.
Bleating: the sound of the kid.
Its owners: its masters.

When the blind Tobit heard the voice of the kid he was surprised: where did his wife get the price of the kid! This shows the degree of poverty to which the family of Tobit had come, since they were living on the little necessary food. So Tobit supposed, and feared, that his wife or his son, under the pressure of poverty and need, had stolen this kid; and he asked that it be returned to its owners. Here Tobit's piety, honesty, and adherence to the commandments of God in the midst of affliction appear; he is truly Tobit, the one blessed by God for his holiness.

entries.section: (3) The reproaches of his wife

paragraphs.text: As for Anna his wife, whose name means tenderness, she represents limited human tenderness: she worked to support her family but with distress. In the face of her husband's supposition that the kid was stolen, she became very angry and declared the murmuring that was hidden in her heart, and she reproached her blind husband, declaring the vanity of his hope and his almsgiving, since God had left him to fall into this hard trial. Nevertheless, St. Tobit bore her words, steadfast in his faith.

Here the difference appears between accepting the trial from God and merely enduring it because there is no escape from it. In the first case, a person feels the help of God strengthening him in the trial, and feels an inner peace and receives abundant blessings. This is what Tobit did. In the second case, a person endures because there is no other alternative, and relies not on God but on himself, so he falls into distress, depression, murmuring and sometimes despair, and wrongs others. This is what Anna, the wife of Tobit, did.
Hold fast to God in affliction and in ease, and enjoy His fellowship at all times; then you will not feel distress all your life.
The prayers of Tobit and Sara, and the death of Sara's seven husbands

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobit

paragraphs.text: When the affliction on Tobit increased, he did not sin against God or against men, but expressed his feelings and cast all his burden upon God, in a prayer full of feelings of sorrow and groaning from the affliction, and he mingled his prayer with his tears. It was a prayer from the heart. And he offered a complete prayer that included:

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobit

paragraphs.text: 1- Glorifying God, for he ascribed to Him justice, uprightness, mercy, truth and wisdom.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobit

paragraphs.text: A byword: he became a subject of men's mockery and talk.

2- Confession in repentance of sin, not only his own sins, but the sins of his fathers, their failure to keep the commandments of God, the impure heart and the unclean intention. These sins led to their falling into captivity and their being exposed to plunder and killing; indeed they became a reproach and a worthless people, despised.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobit

paragraphs.text: 3- Under the pressure of the affliction upon him, he asked that God would permit and command that his life be ended, that he might be delivered from these troubles. But he set a condition for his request, that it be according to the will of God. Here trust in God and submission to Him appear.

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: Sara: a Hebrew word meaning princess.
Raguel: a Hebrew word meaning friend of God.

This family was bound to God in love and friendship, as appears from this book. Sara was distinguished in her relationship with God, as a princess. She lived in a small city near the city of Rages in the land of the Medes, which the Assyrians had taken, and to which they had transferred some Jews, as we mentioned earlier. Because the city of Raguel was near Rages, it was called by its name, Rages being taken to include the great city and the surrounding country. On the very day when Tobit heard a reproach from his wife Anna, Sara heard a reproach from one of her father's maidservants. This shows that Raguel was a rich man, with a large house and maidservants.

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: Asmodeus: the name of a Persian pagan god. The name Asmodeus means the spirit of violence and destruction, or the spirit of sexual lust.

The reason for the maidservant's reproach of her mistress was that Sara had been married, and on the wedding night, as soon as her husband entered the chamber to be united with her, a demon named Asmodeus attacked him. (All the gods of the Gentiles are demons.) He represents cruelty, violence, and the killing of the husband. This happened seven times, that is, the devil killed seven husbands who tried to be united with Sara. Perhaps they were from the Gentiles. The number seven represents completeness, which shows the authority of the devil. Perhaps Sara's husbands were not of the people of God, that is, they were pagans, unbelievers, or Jews who did not hold fast to the faith and the commandments of God. Whoever they were, the reason for their union with her was bodily lust and the wealth that she enjoyed.

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: When one of the maidservants erred in some task, her mistress Sara rebuked her, and the maidservant answered her insolently, with false accusations, and reproached her that she had failed in marriage seven times and therefore had borne neither a son nor a daughter like other women. She also falsely accused her of being the killer of the seven husbands, a thing that even ordinary logic rejects: why would a bride kill the bridegroom with whom she rejoiced to be united?

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: The maidservant also accused her mistress of attempting to kill her, by asking: Do you want to kill me?

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: Because the reproach was severe, Sara was greatly distressed and went up to a room on the upper floor (an upper chamber) and stayed in it three days and three nights, tasting no food, in continual fasting and prayer with tears, that God might take away her reproach.

In ancient times the devout Jews would sometimes build on the roofs of their houses a small room, in which they spent some time in worship and prayer. They made windows for this room facing the direction of the temple in Jerusalem, even in the days of the captivity, that they might remember the temple of God and offer worship to Him. This upper room is mentioned in the life of Daniel (Dan 6:10, 11) and also in the life of Judith (Jdt 9:1). We also note the upper room of the house of St. Mark, in which Christ gathered with His disciples and instituted the sacrament of the Eucharist, and in which He also appeared after His resurrection and the Holy Spirit came upon them (Mk 14:15, Acts 1:13). Tears show the intensity of her sorrow. Tears are repeated often in this book, which shows the tenderness of feeling and the strength of emotion in the characters who appear in it, whether in sorrow or in joy. These are the occasions on which tears are mentioned in this book:-
1- Tobit's weeping at the feast when he rose to bury one of the dead Jews (ch. 2:7).
2- Tobit's tears in his prayer, after he lost his sight (ch. 3:1).
3- Sara's weeping, after her maidservant's reproach of her (ch. 3:10).
4- The weeping of Tobias's mother over him, after his parting from her and his journey to recover the value of the bond (ch. 5:18).
5- The weeping of Raguel and his wife Anna and their daughter Sara, when they met and came to know the younger Tobias (ch. 7:6-8).
6- The weeping of Anna, Sara's mother, at the marriage of her daughter, for fear of Tobias's death (ch. 7:16).
7- The weeping of Gabael on meeting Tobias in the house of Raguel, rejoicing at meeting him (ch. 9:6).
8- The weeping of Anna, Tobias's mother, because of Tobias's delay in returning from his journey (ch. 10:3, 7).
9- The weeping of Tobit and Anna his wife at the return of their son Tobias (ch. 11:9, 13).

entries.section: (2) Sara the daughter of Raguel and the death of her seven husbands

paragraphs.text: It was a prayer without murmuring, for Sara blessed God in it.

God is a refuge for His children who believe in Him. When Anna reproached Tobit her husband, he hurried to prayer and did not quarrel with his wife, nor did he take refuge in human beings who were unable to help him. So also Sara hurried to be alone with God in fasting and prayer, in the face of her maidservant's reproaches and accusations. God is our heavenly Father, and His door is always open to us with love and tenderness, to hear our prayers and help us in our afflictions, and even to remove them from us and give us comfort and peace during the affliction and all the days of our life. May we hurry to God like these two saints, Tobit and Sara, and find our rest in the Church and her sacraments, that is, in confession, Communion and all the means of grace, especially prayer and the Holy Bible.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: 1- Her humility and her confession of her sin, and also her hope in the merciful God, who, though He permits some affliction, returns to have mercy and lift the trial.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: 3- Her asking God to take away the shame that wearies her in soul and humiliates her, or to end her life on earth according to His will. This shows the degree of distress she was suffering.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: Then the devout Sara declares here her holding fast to a life of chastity, as a maiden before marriage.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: And likewise her withdrawal from reckless young men who love corrupt worldly amusements.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: Also, when she accepted marriage her aim was not bodily lust but the forming of a family in the fear of God. Because of the purity of her heart, the devil Asmodeus was not able to touch her with harm while he killed her husbands, and this confirms that they came to marriage only for the purpose of bodily lust.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: In humility and submission to the will of God, she accepted the failure of her seven previous marriages, for she believes that they were not suitable for her, and in humility she says that she was not worthy of them. And in hope she awaits the man whom God prepares as a suitable husband for her.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: Finally Sara declares her faith in the loftiness of God's wisdom.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: And although God permits chastening, all His children trust that He returns to rescue them and have mercy on them. For God desires and rejoices in the salvation of His children and not their destruction, and is pleased with their joy and rejoicing, so He permits the affliction in order to give them joy afterward.

entries.section: (3) The prayer of Sara

paragraphs.text: He deserves blessing and honor forever. Thus Sara ends her prayer with the glorification of God and submission to Him.

Sara is an example for the balanced young person, who cares for a life of purity in all his conduct and speech, even if he sacrifices some impure friends, however dear they are, and even if he sacrifices some amusements and gatherings that make a person lose his purity. My young brethren, and every person, are you careful in your life to keep purity and to enjoy fellowship with God and His love?

And do the young people who are approaching marriage follow the thinking and conduct of Sara? Let the basis of choice not be built on outward beauty, desires and material things, but let it be the choice of the person who works to form a Christian family and develops the relationship with God, so that we may enjoy feelings of pure love in intimacy and affection in union with Christ Jesus.

entries.section: (4) The answering of the prayers of Tobit and Sara

paragraphs.text: Here fervent prayers appear, springing from the heart, which the angels immediately lift up before the throne of the great God in heaven, and we see how God answers these prayers with concern, for He sent the great archangel Raphael to resolve the affliction of each of them and heal him of his troubles.

entries.section: (4) The answering of the prayers of Tobit and Sara

paragraphs.text: Raphael: one of the three great archangels, Michael, Gabriel and Raphael. The meaning of his name is the compassion of God.

This shows not only God's love and tenderness toward us, but also the love of the angels and their service to us. The Church celebrates the angel Raphael on the third day of the Little Month (Nasie). St. John Chrysostom says that on this day the angel Raphael appeared to the disciples of Christ. There is another feast of the angel Raphael, in remembrance of the building of the first church in his name, which was built by King Arcadius on the shore of the Bosphorus; this feast falls on the 13th of Koiak.
Tobit's charge to his son

entries.section: (1) Honoring his mother

paragraphs.text: Thought: supposed.

After Tobit prayed, his heart was at ease, and he felt that God would answer him and deliver him from his affliction. This shows his strong faith, but he imagined, or supposed, that his deliverance from the affliction would be by the ending of his life. (God did indeed answer, but He appointed another solution to his affliction, by healing him of his illness, as will appear later.)

How happy is the person who believes that God answers his prayer, for his heart is at rest and is assured that he has cast his problem, indeed his whole life, into the faithful hand that cares for him and loves him more than he loves himself, namely the tender hand of God. And in proportion as he directs his heart in prayer toward God in all his needs, he feels a peace that surpasses all understanding and enjoys a constant joy.

entries.section: (1) Honoring his mother

paragraphs.text: Therefore Tobit called his son to give him his last charge, which was very precious counsel that every person needs, for it represents the essence of the thought of St. Tobit, who asked his son to make it the foundation of his life.

entries.section: (1) Honoring his mother

paragraphs.text: The faith of Tobit the father was that it is God who will take his spirit at death, and this is the faith of all the children of God. He then charged his son to bury his body.

entries.section: (1) Honoring his mother

paragraphs.text: Then he charged him to honor his mother, reminding him of what she had endured for him in conceiving and giving birth and in all her care of him. This is what every person ought to remember, remembering all that his parents endured for him, so that he hurries to honor them, carrying out the commandment of God, and continues so all the days of their lives, and after this buries them with honor.

entries.section: (1) Honoring his mother

paragraphs.text: The father charged that his wife's body be buried beside his own, and this shows his love for her, even after death, forgetting her anger and her reproach of him and all her faults. For love forgets offense and forgives.

My brother, may you forgive others their faults quickly, so that your heart may be cleansed and love may be the ruling power in your feelings toward them, and consequently you may care for them and honor them, and enjoy through all this a peace and joy that never cease.

entries.section: (2) Almsgiving and its blessings

paragraphs.text: Then he began to charge him with specific matters, the first of which is almsgiving. If he loves God and is satisfied with His care, he will not accept sin, because it is a breaking of the commandment of God, whom he loves with all his heart. Thus he can give up his selfishness and his anxiety about himself, and love others and care for them and give them the utmost he can of his money and effort.

entries.section: (2) Almsgiving and its blessings

paragraphs.text: Then he declared to him clearly that he should be merciful and not neglect the poor, lest God neglect him and not hear his petition.

entries.section: (2) Almsgiving and its blessings

paragraphs.text: He asked him to give according to what he has: if he is rich, to give much, and if he is poor, to give little, but willingly, not attached to money or anxious about his needs.

entries.section: (2) Almsgiving and its blessings

paragraphs.text: Then he promises him the blessings of almsgiving, for it has a great reward with God. Because of almsgiving God has mercy on him and keeps him far from sin, so that he does not fall into it, and forgives him if he falls, and directs his heart to repentance, and rescues him from death and eternal perdition. Almsgiving gives a firm hope in blessed eternity.

It is noted here that when the aged Tobit lost his sight, his inner sight flourished and grew strong within him, so that he was able, with the guidance of the Holy Spirit, to give all these commandments to his son. The son was seeing with his outward eyes, yet he needed the guidance of his father who had lost his sight. Tobit the father speaks with confidence about the importance of almsgiving, which delivers from darkness, that is, eternal torment. This means that he is not troubled by the darkness of his outward eyes, but his heart is attached to the heavenly light in the eternal Kingdom. Therefore he charges his son to care for almsgiving, which brings him to the Kingdom, and not to be occupied, like the rest of men, with material possessions.

How great it is to give although what you have is little, even feeling your poverty and material need. For giving is a departure from selfishness and complete trust in the care of God, who blesses the giver with countless blessings. Look at the woman who gave the two mites, and how much the Lord Christ praised her more than all the rich who gave. Giving out of want is the glory of all gifts.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: Then he warned him against two great sins. The first is the sin of fornication: let him be content with his relationship with his wife, and have no excuse to look at, or think of, or desire another woman, because in this there is covetousness and a treating of sin as permissible. He warned him not to run after any new knowledge of sin in all its corrupt forms.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: The second sin against which he warned him is the sin of pride, whether in words or even only in thought, because pride is behind all sins and is the chief motive of the sin of fornication. The proud man gives up his carefulness and falls into fornication, whereas God guards the humble from fornication and all sins.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: Then the father continues with a group of commandments, the first of which is that he pay the hired man his wages at once. This is an application of the commandment of faithfulness and mercy, for the hired man is in need of what he worked for. Therefore delaying the wages is an exploitation of another's money without right, and counts as theft and covetousness.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: Then he set before him a principle in all his dealings with others: that what he hates for people to do to him, he is not to do to anyone. This verse, and many other verses, were quoted in the New Testament.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: Then he stresses almsgiving again, but from another understanding: almsgiving is not only to clothe the naked, but also to eat with the poor of what he gives them in alms, in a fellowship of love, whether in a visit to them or on occasions of condolence. It seems that it was common in ancient times, as it is now, to offer alms for the souls of the departed, given to the poor and needy. So he charged him to eat with the poor, but not to mingle with the wicked or eat with them of these foods.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: He spoke in the spirit of prophecy about the sacrifice of the New Testament, that is, the bread and wine placed on the altar, which is a type of the tomb of the righteous Christ; they become the most holy Body and Blood of the Lord, and all who hunger and thirst after righteousness eat of them, and sinners who do not repent do not eat of them.

The Law of the Old Testament forbade approaching or touching tombs, so Tobit here speaks in the spirit of prophecy about the blessing of the bodies of the saints in the New Testament. As for the direct meaning of this verse in the Old Testament, it is the distribution of alms (bread and wine) in the name of the righteous man who died, that the needy may eat of them.

entries.section: (3) Commandments for dealing with others

paragraphs.text: Then he asks him for spiritual discipleship at the hands of the wise, that he may hear the counsel of God from their mouths, and then calls him to humility and to seeking the counsel of God in all his affairs, so that he blesses and thanks God, who guides him and cares for him.

entries.section: (4) Recovering the debt from Gabael

paragraphs.text: Finally he gave his son a material charge. Although the father was detached and ascetic, accepting poverty willingly, yet with the tenderness of fatherhood he took pity on his son and wished to provide him with some material comfort. So he charged him to recover the silver that he had lent to Gabael, of which he had a bond (Tob 1:17). In ancient times bonds were written on a piece of skin or clay, and then burned so that the clay would set and become dry and strong. There were two ways of writing bonds:
1- Two identical bonds are written, and the creditor and the debtor each take a copy of it.

2- One bond is written and divided into two halves, and the creditor and the debtor each take a part of the bond. This is what happened in the book of Tobit according to the longer text in the fifth chapter.
Bonds are mentioned in the Old Testament with Jeremiah (Jer 32:9-14) and in the New Testament in the parable of the unjust steward (Lk 16).

entries.section: (4) Recovering the debt from Gabael

paragraphs.text: Then he reassured his son that the children of God, although they live in poverty, have good awaiting them in eternity, on condition that they avoid sin and care to do good.
The meeting with the angel and his journey with the younger Tobias

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: The younger Tobias is distinguished by the virtue of swift and complete obedience.

As the longer text mentions to us, twenty years had passed since the writing of this bond, and the bond was written when the younger Tobias was a child, so the younger Tobias is now in his twenties. He is a type of Christ, who obeyed the Father by His Incarnation and redemption when He said: "For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me" (Jn 6:38).

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: But because of his young age and little experience in financial dealings, he found before him two problems for which he asked his father for a solution, and this shows his humility and his care to seek counsel. The first problem was how Gabael would give him the money when he did not know him. The second problem was that he did not know the way to the city of Rages.
The younger Tobias is a type of the children of God in their prayer and seeking of God's counsel, and Tobit the father is a type of God, who guides His children and solves their problems.

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: So Tobit the father guided him and explained to him that the bond was a financial document sufficient to make Gabael know him in person and to guarantee him with Gabael, so that he would give him the money.

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: As for the way to Rages, he proposed to his son that he look for a trustworthy man who knew the way, to be a guide for him and accompany him there and receive his wages. This was the method followed for guidance in travel, in a time when the roads were not paved or provided with signs for guidance, as is the case now. Tobit the father wished that this might be done quickly, so that the son might travel and return in the father's lifetime, that he might be assured about him, for he felt that his death was near.

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: The younger Tobias went out to carry out his father's word in looking for a man to guide him on the way to Rages. Since the prayer of Tobit the father had been answered, the son did not have to labor, for as soon as he went out he found a young man with splendor shining on his face, ready for the road and for travel. He greeted him and asked about his race.

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: He informed him that he was of the children of Israel, that is, of the people of God, so Tobias was reassured that he was of his own race. He asked him whether he knew the way to the land of the Medes.

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: He told him that he had traveled all the roads to it, and more than this, he informed him that he had stayed with Gabael, who lived in the city of Rages, the city of the Medes, which is on the mountain of Ecbatana (see Map 2, p. 265).

entries.section: (1) The younger Tobias meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Tobias rejoiced greatly, since he found sufficient signs that made him trust this young man. He was a Jew and knew all the roads of the Medes, and even knew Gabael himself, to whom Tobias wished to go. Tobias did not know that this was the angel of God, Raphael. His saying that he was of the people of God meant that he was one of those near to God, and knew all the roads of travel, and knew Gabael, and dwelt in his house and in all the houses of the children of God. Then the young man asked leave of him, that he might give his father the good news that he had found the guide needed for the way.

The prayer that springs from the heart of one who believes in God, and who has passed through trial with patience and endurance, reaches heaven quickly and is answered at once, and even exceeds what a person asks or thinks. God did not send a man to guide Tobias to the city of Rages, but sent an angel, and not only an angel, but the archangel Raphael, to guide him and accompany him and pour out upon him many blessings from God. Prayer is a door open to us every day, that we may speak with God and feel His presence before us face to face and experience His work and care in the details of our daily life.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: When Tobit the father learned what had happened with his son, he rejoiced and marveled at the swiftness of God's answer to his prayer and His sending of the guide for his son, and he asked that the guide come in to him.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: The young man came in and greeted him and asked for him the grace of God, which He pours out upon His children and which distinguishes them from others, namely constant joy.
The angel Raphael's announcing constant joy to Tobit is a type of the angel's announcing great joy to the shepherds (Lk 2:10, 11).

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Because of his affliction Tobit the father said: How can I have constant joy when I am blind?

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Recovery: healing.
From: with.

So the angel comforted his heart and told him that his healing from his illness was near, and thus he confirmed in the heart of Tobit the father the hope of the end of his affliction, but not by death, rather by healing.
Thus the divine solution may be far from our mind, yet it is better than the human solution, and everyone who has hope and faith in God enjoys it.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Tobit the father asked the young man to accompany his son to Rages and to take his wages when he returned, and he agreed.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: So that the father might be assured, he asked the young man about his lineage.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Azarias: a Hebrew name meaning God helps.
Ananias: a Hebrew name meaning God is tender.

He replied to him that there was no need to know the lineage of a hired man, but so that his heart might be at ease, he was Azarias the son of the great Ananias. It seems that the family of Ananias was a well-known family among the Jews, so the father was reassured. The angel Raphael did not lie here, but took on a character for the sake of accomplishing the divine plan. He used two names by way of metaphor to indicate the mission entrusted to him, for he is the “helper” sent by God the “Tender.”

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Tobit apologized for this question of his, and the angel reassured him that his son would return safely.

God in His tenderness helps us and rescues us from our afflictions; He sent the chief of His angels to help one of His children. So you too are surrounded by angels and saints, so do not fear and do not be troubled, but always ask for their help and aid.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: Provision for the road: preparations for travel.
Tobit the father bade farewell to his son and the young man Azarias in peace, and wished that God would keep them on the road and that His angel would accompany them.
There is nothing better than the company of God in the wilderness of this world, until we reach our goal, which is blessed eternity.

entries.section: (2) Tobit the father meets the angel

paragraphs.text: The younger Tobias took all the preparations he needed for the journey, of food and clothing and all needs, and they are a type of the spiritual weapons that the spiritual striver needs on the road of his striving in order to reach the Kingdom. Tobias bade his parents farewell and began the journey with his companion Azarias.

We expect that the younger Tobias took simple preparations for the journey, because he was poor, and he here is a type of Christ, who took our poverty and need and became incarnate, born in a manger, to be wedded to His Church on the Cross and to raise her by His resurrection and enrich her with His abundant blessings.

entries.section: (3) The mother's feelings after her son's absence and Tobit the father's reassurance of her

paragraphs.text: They departed: that is, they separated, and what is meant is that they went away, or vanished from their sight.

After Tobias and his companion disappeared from the eyes of the mother Anna, her feelings were stirred, expressed in much weeping, because of her sense of losing her son and her anxiety that she would not see him again, and her need of him, she and his father, because of their old age, since the age of Tobit the father had come near to sixty.

entries.section: (3) The mother's feelings after her son's absence and Tobit the father's reassurance of her

paragraphs.text: The mother declared the unimportance of the money which her son would obtain from Gabael.

entries.section: (3) The mother's feelings after her son's absence and Tobit the father's reassurance of her

paragraphs.text: Indeed she showed that her enjoyment of seeing her son before her was the great wealth that compensated her for her poverty.

Tobit the father is a type of the Father who sent His only-begotten Son into the world (typified by the younger Tobias) to recover the lost money (that is, man, who was lost by sin and condemned to death).

How much the Christian family needs now to feel the importance of love and affection among its members, and that their enjoying one fellowship in Christ Jesus is better than all the material things of the world and its lusts, so that they hold fast to their relationships with one another, in friendship and affection, unconcerned about what they lack of the world's material things that others have. For love is truly a wealth better than all the delights of the world.

entries.section: (3) The mother's feelings after her son's absence and Tobit the father's reassurance of her

paragraphs.text: As for the father Tobit, who enjoyed a strong faith, he felt the emotion of motherhood and its anxiety, so he reassured her that her son would return safely and that the angel of the Lord would keep him until he returned rejoicing. He asked her to stop weeping, and she stopped weeping.

When Tobit the father asked that God send His angel to accompany his son and guide him, we find a swift answer from God, who made his guide an archangel and not merely an angel. How great is God's love and care for His children.
The journey of Tobias and the angel to Rages

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: Lodging: a night, or a stopping place, or a resting place.

Tobias and the angel began their journey from the city of Nineveh, which is on the River Tigris, alongside the river (see ch. 1:16, Map 2, p. 526). When night fell upon them, they spent the first night beside the river, with Tobias's dog with them, which points to the friendship of man with animals, as it was anciently in the Garden of Eden, where there was complete friendship between man and all the animals. Tobias is a type of Christ, who loves all creation and is continually surrounded by angels.

The dog's following Tobias is a type of the salvation of Christ offered to the Jews and the Gentiles, because the Gentiles in the eyes of the Jews are dogs, as Christ expressed in the story of the Canaanite woman (Mt 15:21-28). Tobias, who is a type of Christ, married Sara the Jewess, who is a type of the Church, and the dog also followed him. Then we shall see later (ch. 11:9) how the dog was a herald to Tobit the father and his wife of the return of their son, who is a type of Christ the Redeemer, as the Magi announced to Herod and the Gentiles in their lands the birth of the Savior (Mt 2). Tobias's first descent was beside the River Tigris, and this descent is a type of Baptism, because it is the first entrance into the Church.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: In the morning Tobias wanted to wash in the river, so he went a little way into its water and was startled by a great fish attacking him.

Tobias's going down to wash his feet is a type of Christ, the representative of humanity, who bore our sins and was washed on our behalf in the waters of the Jordan, and likewise washed the feet of His disciples, as a symbol of their being washed from the filth of sin by His redemption.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: Tobias cried out, calling for help to his companion Azarias, calling him my lord, that is, my master, he who has authority over my leading and guarding: the monster, or the great fish, has attacked me.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: The angel guided him to seize the fish by its gills and pull it out of the river, and it would not be able to harm him. As we know, fish breathe by their gills, so when he seized the fish by its gills and drew it to the shore, he stopped its breathing, for it breathes the air dissolved in the water; so it began to suffocate, and this appeared in the flapping of its tail on the ground of the shore at Tobias's feet, until it died.

The monster that attacked Tobias is a type of the affliction that attacks the children of God, but by obedience to God (His angel) and spiritual striving (seizing the fish by its gills and drawing it to the shore), the spiritual man overcomes the affliction, and it does not harm him, but God turns it into a blessing in his life, as you will see. The great fish, that is, the whale, points to Satan our enemy, who goes about seeking whom he may devour, and who attacked Tobias, who is a type of every person who believes in God. When Tobias drew it out of the sea, which points to the world and all its material things, it nearly suffocated, because the power of the devil lies in enticing us with the lusts of the world and its material things. Therefore by detachment and asceticism the devil loses his power and authority over us, and by obedience to God and His commandments, which are represented here by the angel's guidance of Tobias, Satan falls prostrate at our feet.

As Tobias went down into the sea, so Christ went down into the world by His Incarnation. As the monster attacked Tobias, and he bound it by its gills and came out of the sea alive, triumphing over it, with the angel's help, so when Christ prayed in the garden of Gethsemane an angel came to strengthen Him, and by the death of the Cross He trampled death, defeated Satan, and rose alive on the third day.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: Then the angel told Tobias to cut open the belly of the whale, that is, the great fish, and take out its heart, its gall and its liver, for they are useful.

The cutting open of the whale, that is, the great fish, is a type of the piercing of Christ in His side, from which came out blood and water that gave salvation to humanity. Likewise, when Tobias cut open the whale he took out the liver and the gall, and with them he bound Satan and gave healing to his father's eyes. The liver and the heart that Tobias took out he burned later at his marriage to Sara (ch. 8:2), and so he bound Satan and drove him away from them. Likewise in the Mosaic sacrifices the liver was burned on the altar (Lev 3:5) as a type of the death of Christ on the Cross, so that Satan is bound.

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: As for the flesh of the fish, he roasted a part of it for them to eat on the same day or the next, and the rest of the fish's flesh he salted, so that it might last a long time and they might live on it throughout the journey until they reached Rages. The roasted flesh of the fish and the salting of the rest is a type of the peace offering (Lev 7:15-19), a part of which was burned on the altar and whose flesh was also salted and eaten by the one who offered it; it is also a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the altar, which we eat as Body and Blood. It is a sacrifice that has nothing to do with bearing sin, but is food for the children of God.

Thus the blessings of affliction appear in the use made of the fish in various ways, the first of which is eating its flesh, not only on the same day, but for a long time. If the affliction is temporary, its blessings extend over many times in a person's life. As salt preserves the flesh of the fish, so pain and weariness (that is, the salty taste) preserve a person's life from many sins, and as the Scripture says: "he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin" (1 Pet 4:1).

entries.section: (1) The killing of the great fish and the use of its organs

paragraphs.text: Tobias asked the angel about the organs of the fish which he had told him to keep, and he said to him that if the heart is burned with fire, its smoke puts an end to every power of the demons, and the gall is useful for healing the eyes. The angel said the same thing about the liver of the whale, that is, the fish, in the same chapter (v. 19), and because of Tobias's obedience Satan was indeed bound. The effect of these organs was not due to a power latent in them, but because of the work of God in them for the sake of the obedience of His children.

The burning of the liver and the heart is a type of the death of Christ. As by their burning and the rising of their smoke the demons were driven out, so by the death of Christ on the Cross His sacrifice rose as a sweet-smelling incense and Satan was bound. As for the gall, it is secreted as a juice in the body, which helps to digest food so that the living being does not fall ill. It is a type of medicine, therefore God used it to treat the illness of the eyes. The gall also points to trials, which cleanse the soul of its sins and prove it before God.

Christ bore the bitterness of our sins on the Cross, and the gifts of the Magi, among which was myrrh, pointed to it. He drank the myrrh and endured the sufferings, so that by His bearing this bitterness He might give us redemption and healing from our sins, as the gall healed the eye of Tobit the father.

Of course these spiritual meanings that the divine inspiration presents are entirely different from incantations and works of magic, in which the devil tries to imitate the works of God, claiming through sorcerers and charlatans that he heals the diseases and problems of men.

entries.section: (2) The angel's advice to Tobias to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: At last Tobias and the angel reached the region of Rages (see Map 2, p. 20), a small city near the city of Rages, after a long journey that lasted many days. Tobias asked the angel, that is, the young man Azarias, for he still did not know until now that he was the angel of the Lord, but he was the leader of the journey and his guide, and he asked him where they would stay in this city.

entries.section: (2) The angel's advice to Tobias to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Azarias pointed to the house of Raguel, the father of Sara, for he was a Jew, one of the captives transferred to Rages, and indeed of the tribe of Nephthali and a relative of Tobias.

The name Raguel means friend of God, and he is a type of John the Baptist, who said of himself that he was the friend of the bridegroom (Jn 3:29) and rejoiced at seeing Christ, the Bridegroom and Savior of humanity, as Raguel rejoiced at seeing Tobias and at his marriage to his daughter.

entries.section: (2) The angel's advice to Tobias to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Raguel was a rich man and had only one daughter. Azarias guided Tobias to ask for her in marriage and told him that Raguel would accept, so that he would receive the blessing of marriage to a devout maiden and also obtain much money. The angel Raphael here, in choosing Sara as a wife for Tobias, resembles Eliezer of Damascus, who brought Rebekah to be a wife for Isaac (Gen 24). Sara's wealth points to the spiritual blessings with which God pours out upon His devout children. In the Old Testament God expressed His blessings in a material form, according to the understanding of the people at that time; but in the New Testament, after the revelation of the knowledge of God, we no longer need material blessings as an expression of spiritual blessings, although God gives them to whoever needs them, if this is good for him.

The archangel here is a type of the Holy Spirit in marrying Tobias to Sara, as He marries the Church to Christ her Redeemer, so that she becomes a bride to Him forever, and as Eliezer of Damascus did in marrying Rebekah to Isaac (Gen 24), especially since the name of each has a beautiful meaning: Azarias, who is the angel Raphael, has a name meaning God helps, and Eliezer has a name meaning God helps.
The angel Raphael is also a type of John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Christ, to redeem His bride the Church.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: Since Sara was among Tobias's relatives, and in addition Tobit the father used to travel through the various lands of the empire to help needy Jews, the younger Tobias had received the news of Sara's marriage to seven husbands and the devil's killing of each of them on the wedding night. Christ said of the devil that he was a murderer from the beginning (Jn 8:44), and Tobias declared to the angel his fear that he too would be killed, being the only son of his parents, and that they would grieve over him all the days of their lives.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: They cast out: from banishment, that is, they put away and neglect.

Here the angel made clear to Tobias an important truth, which is that the devil has power only over those who marry for lust alone, and who are thereby far removed from God. They are like the animals, which mate by instinct alone, and in which there is no spirit that loves God and does everything for His sake.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: So that Tobias might be safe if he married Sara, the archangel Raphael charged him to keep away from the bodily relationship, if he went in to her in the chamber on the wedding night, but rather that the two of them should pray for the first three days and live together in spiritual love.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: On the first night he is to burn the liver of the whale (not present in the verse, but mentioned earlier, Tob 6:8), and this is a type of the redemption of Christ, as we mentioned, so that the devil is defeated and bound and does not come near them, for by their chastity and their prayers they show that their purposes in marriage were nothing but their love for one another in God.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: On the second night they receive the blessing of their fellowship with the saints, and this points to membership in the Church and the forming of a new family in the body of Christ, that is, the Church.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: On the third night they receive the blessing of fatherhood and motherhood, that they may be granted healthy children.

entries.section: (3) The reply to Tobias's fears

paragraphs.text: After the third night, they are joined in a bodily relationship as children of God, living in His fear and in love for one another, for this relationship is not mere bodily lust, and the blessing of the holy fathers, represented by Abraham the father of fathers, will be with them.

On the basis of this scriptural text, the Church has arranged in her rite that the couple on the day of the crowning be bound with a red girdle (a band of cloth) tied in the form of a cross, which points to their union together in Christ by the sacrament of Matrimony, which is from the blessings of the blood of Christ the Redeemer (the red color). After three days of their union in the sacrament of Matrimony, and after offering prayers of thanksgiving for three days, the rite of the untying of the girdle is performed for them, that is, after their abiding in Christ, who gave them this sacrament by His death on the Cross, and they were united together in a lofty union, in which mere bodily lust dies with the death of Christ. On the third day, that is, the day of Christ's resurrection, the girdle is untied, and the couple begin a new life, in which they practice their bodily relationship with a new understanding, for it is not mere bodily lust, but an expression of their union together in Christ and of a self-giving love for one another.
The marriage of Tobias to Sara

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: The angel and Tobias reached the house of Raguel and went in to him, and he received them with welcome and joy. This shows that he possessed the virtue of hospitality to strangers, and so we see God's blessings upon the devout who love virtue. Raguel, by his love for all people and his hospitality to strangers among them, gained a great blessing in the solution of the problem of his life, namely the death of the husbands of his only daughter, for God sent him his devout relative Tobias to marry her and beget a righteous offspring. Thus everyone who strives to acquire a virtue is led by it to other virtues and abundant blessings from God, and it also lifts from him his various afflictions.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: The acquaintance began between the members of the household and the guests, and before Raguel spoke with them, he noticed the great resemblance in appearance between the young man before him and his relative Tobit the father, and he whispered this to his wife Anna. The longer text of the book says that Raguel was the cousin of Tobit the father.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Then Raguel asked the two young men about their origin and where they lived, and they told him that they were of the captives of the tribe of Nephthali, who were carried away to the city of Nineveh, the capital of Assyria (see Map 2, p. 265).

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Raguel asked at once: Do you know Tobit my brother? This makes clear that he was not merely a relative of his from his tribe and kindred, but also very dear to his heart, in addition to the spiritual and worldwide standing of Tobit the father. They answered that they knew him.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Raguel rejoiced and began to speak about his relative, whom he called my brother because of the closeness of the kinship, and to praise his many virtues. After much speaking about the virtues of Tobit, the angel said that this Tobit of whom you speak is the father of this young man before you, indicating the younger Tobias.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: When Raguel heard that the young Tobias before him was the son of his beloved Tobit the father, and he had noticed the resemblance between them at the beginning of the meeting, he rejoiced greatly and hurried to embrace Tobias, and from the excess of his joy he wept much.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Anna wept too, and Sara likewise, and Raguel went on praising Tobias and blessed him, because he was the son of the righteous man of many virtues.

The younger Tobias is a type of Christ, who came down to our earth (the house of Raguel) by His Incarnation, and the devout received Him with joy, namely Joseph the carpenter with the Virgin Mary, and the shepherds and the Magi. After many days (the long conversation) which He spent on our earth, our redemption was accomplished on the Cross, to blot out the penalty of death due to us. Thus He bought us with His blood as a bride for Himself, that we might live with Him a new life, full of peace and joy forever. Sara also represents the Church condemned to death, whom Christ redeemed and who became His bride. The younger Tobias learned of Sara's problem and came to marry her, so that she might be delivered from her shame and begin a new life with him. In this he is a type of Christ, who knows our pains and the death decreed against us, and became incarnate and came to us and redeemed us on the Cross, to save us.

God feels for you and cares for your prayers and arranges your salvation at the proper time, to lift your pains from you, not only the bodily ones, but, more important, the salvation of your soul and your eternal life. So do not be troubled if the pains increase, or if the answer to your prayers is delayed.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Banquet: a feast.

After the warm meeting between Tobias and the family of Raguel, they sat and talked at length, each telling the other about his life, and they rejoiced at one another's news. Then Raguel ordered a ram to be slaughtered and the food prepared for the guests. The ram here points to the sacrifices of the Old Testament, whose blood was a type of the sacrifice of Christ, but the redemption had to be accomplished by the death of Christ Himself, that is, by the marriage of Tobias, who enters into death (the chamber) and binds Satan, and then comes out alive with his bride, the Church, to the new life.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Despite Raguel's great welcome, the embracing, the weeping and the preparation of the feast, Tobias was not distracted from his goal which the angel had charged him with, and he asked Raguel to give him his daughter in marriage. Tobias here represents the spiritual man, who is not distracted from his goal, which is eternity, by the vain pleasures of the world, or the servant who is not distracted from seeking the salvation of souls by the conversations and works of this world and its material necessities.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Raguel was afraid when he heard this and trembled. This shows Raguel's love for those around him; he was not selfish, for he gave up his joy in his daughter, thinking of the fate awaiting Tobias, his death, like the seven previous husbands.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: While Raguel was afraid and hesitant, Azarias, whose name means God helps, helped him and reassured him to give his daughter to Tobias and that no harm would come to him.
