The death of the seven previous husbands was because they were wicked and lustful, while Tobias is the only one worthy to marry Sara, because he reveres God and fears Him. It is clear from this that whoever reveres God and fears Him receives many blessings, whereas whoever departs from God and is immersed in the lusts of the world loses God's protection of him and is exposed to the warfare of the devil and, in the end, to eternal perdition.

entries.section: (1) Tobias asks to marry Sara

paragraphs.text: Raguel was assured in faith that God had answered his prayers and had at last sent a relative who feared God to marry his daughter, according to the Law of Moses, who commanded that the Jews marry among themselves and among relatives and not from the Gentiles, to preserve the land and the lineages. All these things were a preparation for the coming of the awaited Messiah, Jesus Christ our God, in whom all the types are fulfilled. Then he promised and reassured Tobias that he would give him Sara as a wife.

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: The marriage ceremonies began, and Raguel took the hand of his daughter Sara and gave her to Tobias. This is still the practice today: the father of the bride gives her hand to her betrothed when they enter the church to complete the sacrament of Matrimony, and the priest also gives the bridegroom the hand of his bride before the sanctuary during the completion of the sacrament. In the Old Testament the head of the family performed the work of the priest (since marriage was not yet a sacrament and the sacraments had not yet been instituted).

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: After the marriage was completed spiritually, they wrote a marriage contract and signed it, as proof of what God had accomplished, and this is still in force today.

We note that nothing is said about the dowry, because Tobias was poor and had nothing to offer his bride except himself. He is a type of Christ, who became poor for our sake and offered Himself naked of all the glory of the world on the Cross, and gave Himself as redemption and salvation for His Church.

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: After the marriage was completed they rose and ate from the feast with joy. This often happens now: after the completion of the marriage a feast is held which the couple attend with relatives and loved ones, to express their joy in the work of God. These feasts must differ from the feasts of the people of the world, which are full of displays unsuitable for the children of God, for God's blessing in love feasts cannot agree with displays that anger Him.

The rite of the Church prefers that the crowning be held before the Divine Liturgy, after the raising of the morning incense, so that the bride and bridegroom may partake of the Holy Mysteries, because every sacrament is crowned with the sacrament of the Eucharist, which is the sacrament of sacraments. From here this feast is a symbol of the sacrament of the Eucharist, which takes place after the marriage.

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: After the feast, Raguel ordered a private dwelling to be prepared, that is, a suite including a chamber and its annexes, for the bride and bridegroom. This confirms the spiritual and psychological principle that newlyweds should have a separate dwelling, in which they can cooperate in forming a new family, enjoying oneness and privacy together with their love for their relatives. In ancient times houses were very large, allowing separate suites, like the buildings that exist today containing a group of apartments.

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: Sara went in with Tobias to her chamber with tears in her eyes. They were tears in which the joy of marriage mingled with fear for her bridegroom lest he die, and also tears of awe at the new life.

entries.section: (2) The marriage of Tobias to Sara

paragraphs.text: May He grant you: may He give you.
Anna, Sara's mother, sent her off with words of encouragement and wishes of hope for joy, in place of all her former troubles.

The mother, as she encourages her daughter Sara, is a type of the angel who encourages the Church. The Church is here represented in the person of Christ our God, who carried us in His body and was wrestling for our sake in the garden of Gethsemane, and His sweat was like drops of blood, like the tears of Sara falling from her eyes, and then an angel came to strengthen Him.
Tobias and Sara begin their married life

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: After the wedding feast, that is, the supper, Tobias the husband went into the chamber with his wife. This supper is a type of the Lord's Supper, which Christ held on Holy Thursday, in which He offered His Body and Blood as food for His disciples and His Church.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: A piece: a portion.

As soon as he went in, he remembered the angel's words, so he prepared coals and laid upon them a part of the liver of the fish and also its heart, although it is not mentioned in this verse, but it is understood from what came before (Tob 6:8). Here we see that Tobias uses something material to accomplish a spiritual work, for by the burning of the liver and the heart the angel Raphael bound Satan, as appears in (v. 3). This is what the Church does in her sacraments, taking a material form for the hidden spiritual work of the Holy Spirit: the renewal of man's nature in the sacrament of Baptism takes place under the form of water, and in the sacrament of the Eucharist we receive the Body and Blood of Christ under the form of bread and wine; for we are human beings of spirit and body, and we need something perceptible that the body can touch, while the spirit believes in the work of God.

Because of what Tobias did, kindling coals when he first entered his chamber with his wife, the Church has cared for the rite of blessing houses and raising incense, to sanctify the dwelling of the bride and bridegroom before their marriage and at every other time, to drive away the works of the demons and for the blessing of God to come.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: Bound him: shackled him.

Then the devil Asmodeus could not approach them, and more than this, the archangel Raphael attacked him and seized him and cast him into the desert of Upper Egypt, that is, the desert of the far Sa'id; for Egypt resisted the works of God in the form of Pharaoh and all his people and his soldiers, in the days when the people of God dwelt among them, and God struck them with the ten plagues. We see that demons like to dwell in the deserts far from men, since some of them have a relationship with God in prayer and worship, and Satan cannot bear prayers raised in humility and love of God. In addition, the desert of Upper Egypt, that is, the far Sa'id, is the region of Luxor, which was called Thebes, where the Egyptians worshiped the god Amun and many gods, and idols spread in this region, and there Satan rests; for the Psalm says: "All the gods of the nations are demons" (Ps 96:5). It is understood from this that what Tobias did is not among the works of magic, as some object to this book, because magic is among the works of the demons, but here the binding of Satan is among the works of God. Just as they accused Christ of having a relationship with Beelzebub, and He answered them that if a kingdom is divided against itself it is brought to desolation. So this cannot be a work of satanic magic, but the work of God, who is stronger than the demons and able to bind him (Mt 12:24-30). Thus the blessings of the obedience in which Tobias walked appear, and God rescued him from death. So we too, by our obedience to the commandments of God, are rescued by Him from eternal death.

The younger Tobias here is a type of Christ, and his meeting with Sara in the chamber, and the binding of Satan and his being cast far away in the desert of Egypt, is a type of what happened on the day of Christ's crucifixion. By His death He bound Satan and died for His Church, united with her, to raise her in Himself from death by the resurrection on the third day. This day we can call the day of Golgotha, or Great Friday, while the third day is the day of the Resurrection.
Raphael's seizing of Satan and casting him far from Sara and Tobias is a type of Christ's binding of Satan by His Cross and driving him away from His bride the Church.
May you sanctify your house with many prayers, so that the angels guard it and keep away from it all the deeds of the devil.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: Tobias came forward, as the head of this new family and its leader, and spoke to his wife that they should stand to pray and enjoy union with God through prayer for three days, after the likeness of the Holy Trinity, that is, the perfection of oneness and communion with God. When they are united with God, they are able to be united bodily in a conjugal relationship. This is the conduct of the children of God who are sanctified in Him, where their relationship with God is the basis of all their works.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: The couple rose and prayed a fervent prayer from the heart, that God would keep them in His love, and keep away from them all the works of the devil, and heal them of all spiritual illnesses, that is, forgive their sins.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: The divine inspiration records for us here the prayer of Tobias and Sara, which is considered an excellent model that we offer to every bride and bridegroom at the beginning of their life, to follow it. Tobias raised his heart in praise to God before everything, calling all creation to glorify God with him. For so man was created to be lord of all creation and responsible for leading it in the praise of God.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: Tobias remembered the first marriage in the world, in Paradise before the fall, that is, the marriage of Adam and Eve, wishing that his marriage might be in union with God and a relationship of love and continual prayer.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: Then Tobias declares that lust was not the aim of their marriage, but the begetting of offspring, in whom God is blessed, and this offspring shares in the praise of God. The begetting of offspring in the Old Testament was an important matter, much more than in the New Testament, since everyone hoped that the Messiah would come from his offspring; therefore barrenness was a sign of weakness and lack of blessing. But in the New Testament, marriage is complete in its blessing, even without children; for spiritual sonship is more important, as is the service of God in addition to praise.

entries.section: (1) The prayer of Tobias and Sara and the defeat of Satan

paragraphs.text: As for Sara, she prayed in humility, asking the mercy of God, that He would forgive their sins and uphold them throughout their lives, even to old age; for a long life was a sign of blessing in the Old Testament.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: Throughout the wedding night, both Raguel and his wife Anna kept watch, anxious about Tobias lest he die like the previous husbands. At the crowing of the cock, that is, the time before dawn, before the rising of the daybreak, Raguel gathered some of his servants and workers, and they dug a grave beside the house in which to bury Tobias.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: Raguel feared that what had befallen the previous husbands would befall Tobias, for he believed that Tobias's death was inevitable and that he could not avert it.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: Therefore Raguel ordered a grave to be prepared for Tobias, then asked his wife Anna to send a maidservant to look at the couple in the chamber, for he had a hidden hope that God was able to rescue Tobias.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: The maidservant returned to tell them that she had seen them safe, alive, sleeping quietly, so the parents rejoiced and thanked and blessed the Lord.

Raguel and Anna are a type of the women who saw the Lord Jesus in the tomb and made sure of His death, then at dawn on Sunday, while it was still dark, went to the tomb, and the angel, to whom the maidservant points, met them and told them the good news of the Resurrection. Tobias is a type, as we mentioned, of Christ, and Sara of His Church, which is His body, with which He entered into death and came out alive by His resurrection.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: The parents offered a prayer of thanksgiving to God and called Him the God of Israel, that is, the God who is concerned for His people and His children, because His mercy is wide and He turns away from us the works of the demons, for He is the Almighty and can rescue us from all dangers.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of Raguel and Anna after the deliverance of Tobias

paragraphs.text: And they asked for the couple that they might live with God in a life of thanksgiving, and offer before Him sacrifices of praise, that is, their reasonable worship, in holy prayers and worship, and that God might be glorified in them and they might be a sign to all peoples, for there is no other god on earth but the God of Israel.

entries.section: (3) The feast of joy and Raguel's gifts to Tobias

paragraphs.text: After the announcement of the good news of the new life which God had bestowed on the couple, every trace of death had to be removed, so Raguel filled in the grave before dawn, which points to the Resurrection, for death had ended with the darkness of the night. The filling in of the grave also is a type of the end of the authority of Hades over the children of God, whom He raised with Himself, as the empty tomb was proof of the resurrection of Christ on the third day.

entries.section: (3) The feast of joy and Raguel's gifts to Tobias

paragraphs.text: Then he asked his wife Anna to prepare a great feast, the details of which, as he mentioned them, declare the extent of his joy and also his wealth, and it was for all the loved ones, that they might rejoice in the work of God. He also asked her to prepare the needs of travel for the couple and those with them.

For the feast he ordered two cows, and the cow points to goodness, giving and motherhood, since it gives milk abundantly to its young. As for the ram, that is, the male of the sheep, it points to obedience. The number of two cows points to the fact that God's redemption and blessings are for both Jews and Gentiles, and to confirm the meaning. As for four rams, they point to the four corners of the earth, that is, the whole world. The symbolic meaning in this feast is that the blessings of God and His overflowing goodness are poured out abundantly on His obedient children, who are subject to Him throughout the world.

entries.section: (3) The feast of joy and Raguel's gifts to Tobias

paragraphs.text: He begged and urged Tobias to stay with them two weeks, that they might rejoice together in the wonderful work of God and live in the joys of marriage, which represent the joys of the Resurrection and the appearances of the Lord Christ. Raguel asked Tobias to stay with him two weeks, and the seven days (a week) point to the completeness of the work of the Holy Spirit, and two weeks to confirm the meaning, that is, the completeness of joy in the work of the Holy Spirit in holy matrimony.
Tobias did not make light of Raguel's oath, so as not to anger God, who hates the breaking of an oath, and out of respect for the wish of Raguel his father-in-law.

entries.section: (3) The feast of joy and Raguel's gifts to Tobias

paragraphs.text: Then Raguel gave Tobias and his daughter Sara half of his money and promised them the other half after his death, and even wrote a bond to this effect. This shows the extent of his love for the couple, his love of giving, and his non-attachment to money.
Thus the blessings of God appear, not only in keeping us from dangers, but He gives us spiritual and material blessings which we cannot imagine.
Azarias recovers the money from Gabael and invites him to the wedding

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: In the face of God's great work with him, in rescuing him from death and his joy in marrying Sara, Tobias felt that all this was thanks to the guidance of the young man Azarias, and he sensed that his tongue could not express the measure of his thanks to him. So Tobias possessed the virtue of gratitude. He was also a humble man, and this is clear from his saying to the angel: If I became your slave, I would not repay your love and your care for me.

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: With the boldness of love, Tobias ventured to ask Azarias, making use of the time, to go to Rages, the large city near them, and to collect the silver from Gabael and give him the bond, and also to invite him to attend the wedding joys.

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: Another virtue that Tobias possessed was esteem for the feelings of others, for he wished not to be late for his parents, lest they be anxious at his delay, for anxiety assails aged parents.

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: On the other hand, Tobias esteemed the feelings of his father-in-law Raguel, who wanted him to stay two weeks with him to rejoice in his marriage. So he is an example of the spiritual man full of virtues.

Do you thank others for all that they offer you, and express by every means your appreciation for any work they do with you, however small? May you be humble, so that you feel the kindness of others toward you, especially the members of your household, even if their anxiety appears in a rebuke or reproach to you, for this springs from their love and attachment to you. Apologize to them and promise them that you will care for their feelings, and offer them more love, for love is the greatest thing in existence.

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: In great love Azarias responded to Tobias's request and prepared himself for the journey with four servants and two camels. He reached Rages and met Gabael, collected the silver from him and gave him the bond. Here God's care appears, in that Gabael had passed his financial crisis and was able to return all the money to its owner. Azarias here is a type of the spiritual man, striving on his journey in the wilderness of this world. He took two camels with him, and the camel here represents endurance of weariness in travel (striving). Two camels point to both inner striving and outer striving, and to confirm the importance of striving. Four servants point to the striving against the warfare of the devil, which comes from all four corners of the earth, that is, all kinds of warfare. When he completed his striving, he achieved his goal, which was the collecting of the money from Gabael, as the striver wins the Kingdom and the eternal inheritance.

Some of the Fathers see that Azarias, or the angel Raphael, is a type of the Holy Spirit, and the four rams are a type of the four Gospels, and the two camels are a type of the Apostles and the evangelists. The angel Raphael preached to Gabael and told him all that he had been commanded by Tobias, who is a type of Christ.

How beautiful is the cooperation between the two companions! They are an example for every two friends or companions who work or serve together: how they cooperate to achieve their goals, without thinking of the amount of weariness they have borne, and hurry together to the required work. Even if one of the two companions is the elder and greater, in humility he accepts to do any work however lowly: here the archangel hurries to collect the money for Tobias, though he is far above all these passing material works. It is love mingled with humility that drives to cooperation.

entries.section: (1) Azarias recovers the money from Gabael

paragraphs.text: When Gabael learned the good news concerning Tobias and his marriage, he hurried with Azarias to congratulate him. Gabael embraced Tobias, who rushed toward him as soon as he entered. Gabael's feelings toward Tobit the father and his son appeared in his tears when he embraced Tobias. So Gabael too possessed the virtue of gratitude and appreciation for the love of Tobit the father, who had stood with him in his financial crisis; therefore he hurried to congratulate his son. Thus the members of the house of Raguel and the neighbors attended the wedding feast, and they are a type of the Jews who believed in Christ and partook of His Body and Blood. As for Gabael, he is a type of the distant Gentiles, like the Magi and all who believed in Christ from among the Gentiles and enjoyed the Holy Sacraments.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of blessing offered by Gabael

paragraphs.text: Gabael asked the blessing of God, who is concerned for His people and His children (the God of Israel), and the reason for the blessing is the goodness and virtues of Tobit the father, for the blessing of fathers comes upon the children, and the children can make use of this blessing and increase in piety, so that greater blessings come upon them. They may also not benefit from it, but it becomes a cause of their judgment, if they do not walk uprightly.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of blessing offered by Gabael

paragraphs.text: And he asked God to pour out His blessing on Sara also, and on the parents Raguel and Anna, and also Tobit the father and his wife Anna.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of blessing offered by Gabael

paragraphs.text: He even asked a blessing for the children whom he hoped God would give to Tobias, and even the children's children and the offspring extending through the years. The birth of sons, as we mentioned, was a great blessing, because everyone was awaiting the birth of the awaited Messiah from his offspring. All these blessings he asked from God, the King forever and ever, the Almighty, who is able to give a continual blessing; therefore the hearts of the children of God are at ease, because they are in the care of this great and loving God. All who were gathered answered Amen to this great prayer, wishing with Gabael all these blessings.
How beautiful it is to offer prayers and wishes of blessing for all those around us and to encourage them by them, so that they are filled with hope.

entries.section: (2) The prayer of blessing offered by Gabael

paragraphs.text: In expression of joy, everyone came forward to eat from the feast (the wedding feast), which extended throughout the two weeks that Tobias spent with Raguel after his marriage. Here the marks of the joys of the children of God appear: they are in the fear of God; they feel the presence of God in their midst, so they do not go to excess in displays of material joy, which is incompatible with the presence of God. The feast also is a symbol of the sacrament of Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord, in which the faithful rejoice, and which they receive with reverence, fear and great awe. The anxiety of Tobias's parents, and the farewell of Sara and Tobias

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: The feelings of fatherhood and motherhood appear in the waiting of Tobias's parents for him. When he was slow beyond the expected time of his return, because of his marriage and the wedding feasts that continued two weeks, his parents became anxious, and Tobit the father began to think what might be the reasons for his delay.

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: He said: Perhaps he is still looking for Gabael, or Gabael has died.

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: They went on: they remained and continued.
From the intensity of emotion and anxiety the parents wept.

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: Our posterity: our offspring who succeeds us and speaks of us after our death.

A woman is distinguished by her more intense emotion than a man, so the mother Anna expressed her tense emotions, because of her son's delay, with many tears and words that show the feelings of aged parents toward their only young son. She felt that her son was the light of her eyes and her husband's; for in his vitality as a young man he can move quickly and see many things and teach his parents what they cannot reach. He is the helper and aid to his aged parents, who are weak in movement, in meeting their needs. And as the ability of the old to move diminishes, along with their indifference to material things, the movement and accomplishments of the son become an extension of their life and a consolation to them. He is also their hope and the fulfiller of the hopes which they could not fulfill in their lifetime, and even when they think of their death, they see the life of their son and his children as an extension of their life on earth.
These are the feelings of parents who love their children; how much ought children to appreciate these feelings?

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: The mother began to regret sending their son on this mission, for with her anxiety at his delay and the possibility of losing him, she felt that his mere presence was entirely sufficient, and that they had no need of his journey or of collecting the money.
How beautiful it is for a person to be content with what he has and thank God for it, even if the fulfillment of some of what he wants is delayed.

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: Tobit the father tried to reassure his wife that their son would return safely and that the man accompanying him was trustworthy.

entries.section: (1) Anna's grief over her son and Tobit the father's comforting of her

paragraphs.text: She watched: she observed.

But the mother's anxiety dominated her, so she went out every day to look at the roads leading to Nineveh, in case her son might be coming by one of them. This shows that if a person yields to thoughts of anxiety, he does not benefit from the reassuring words of God, so he should take refuge in God by prayer, and He will lift the anxiety from him and reassure him.

entries.section: (2) Raguel's attempts to keep Tobias

paragraphs.text: Send: dispatch.

Raguel, out of his love for his daughter and for Tobias her husband, tried to keep them, so that he and his wife might enjoy their presence with them for a longer period, after the two weeks of the joyful feasts. So he proposed a new idea to Tobias, which was that he send a messenger from himself to Tobit his father, that he and his wife might be reassured of the safety of their son and be told of his marriage.

Raguel here is a type of the disciples of Christ and all His loved ones, who wished that Christ would remain with them on earth, that they might see Him with their eyes, but He made clear to them that He must ascend to heaven, for this was better for them, that they might live by faith with the help of the Holy Spirit. And Tobias, as we have already said, is a type of Christ. As Tobias insisted on returning to his father, so Christ also insisted on completing the redemption and ascending to His Father in heaven.
As Tobias took Sara his bride with him to his father, so Christ prepared a place for His Church (His bride) and received those who believe in Him into Paradise.

entries.section: (2) Raguel's attempts to keep Tobias

paragraphs.text: But the younger Tobias knew the extent of his parents' attachment to him and their anxiety, because of their old age, so he refused gently, despite Raguel's great urging. This shows that although he esteemed the love of Raguel and his wife, he esteemed his responsibility for his parents and his respect for their feelings, even if their anxiety was excessive.

entries.section: (3) Raguel bids farewell to Tobias and Sara

paragraphs.text: After Raguel's attempt to keep Tobias and Sara for a longer time failed, he was not troubled or angry, because his motive was only love and not clinging to his personal opinion. He gave him Sara his wife and half of his property in servants, maidservants and animals.

Tobias's return to his father after completing his mission is a type of the Son's return to sit at the right hand of His Father after completing the redemption, as Christ says: "I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father" (Jn 16:28).

entries.section: (3) Raguel bids farewell to Tobias and Sara

paragraphs.text: As for Raguel, he bade them farewell with joy, wishing them the company of the angel of God on the road, until they reached Tobias's parents. Raguel and his wife wished to live until they should see the children of Tobias and Sara and rejoice in them. It is beautiful for a person to have a hope and expectation throughout his life. Then the parents kissed their daughter Sara and bade farewell to the couple and those with them, that they might go in peace. In proportion as a person asks for the help of God he finds it: as Tobit the father asked for his son the company of the angel of God on his journey, Raguel also asked the company of the angel of God for him on his return. God answered him, and it was indeed the archangel who accompanied him at every step and took care of him.
It is beautiful that Raguel calls the parents of Tobias parents to the couple, for after marriage the parents-in-law become parents.

May every husband and wife look upon their parents-in-law with a filial regard, hurrying to honor them and be subject to them in humility, while making excuses for them because of their old age, and in appreciation of their toil through the past years in bringing up the son or daughter, and see in the parents-in-law's care for one of them a care for the other, for the couple feel that they are one before God.

entries.section: (3) Raguel bids farewell to Tobias and Sara

paragraphs.text: Then Raguel and Anna gave their last charge to their daughter the bride, that she might walk by it in her new life. It is a very important charge, with its five components, which every new wife should care for and with which the parents charge their daughter the new bride.

The first part of this charge is honoring the parents-in-law, because they have become parents. It is strange that they put the honoring of parents before the relationship with the husband, although the basic relationship is with the husband, and it is the most important thing; but honoring the parents gives a calm atmosphere to the new married life, and even increases their love and care for the couple, in addition to the fact that the parents, because of their old age, ought to be honored in the last of their days.
Then comes the second part of the charge, which is love for the husband, with whom she is united and with whom she has one life; oneness cannot be achieved except by self-giving, sacrificial love.

The third part of the charge is care for the upbringing and nurture of the children whom God will bestow upon them, and the ordering and strengthening of the bonds of love, and the arranging of the relationship of love among the children themselves and between them and their parents, so that the family is bound together by the bond of love; and here the wisdom and love of the mother appear. The fourth part of the charge is the management of the house, which includes providing all the material needs for the husband and children, and care, and offering all this in a gentle and cheerful manner, and trying to avoid any conflict among the members of the family.

Finally we come to the fifth and last part, which is that she keep herself blameless, that is, preserve herself from obvious, evident, stumbling faults, such as evil dispositions. What is meant here is not mere error, for there is no person without sin or blame, but it means the importance of spiritual striving in personal life, that a person may be devout before God, and not forget the salvation of his soul amid the responsibilities of life.

Sara, as we said, is a type of the Church, and her parents-in-law are a type of the Law and the books of the Old Testament with all that is in them, for Christ declared that He came "not to destroy, but to fulfil" (Mt 5:17). The husband is Christ, who began with love, and the Church returned love for love: "We love him, because he first loved us" (1 Jn 4:19). As for the children, they are the faithful, and the Church brings up her children and manages their affairs with all the activities and services in her, and keeps herself in purity, far from sin.
The arrival of Tobias at his parents and the healing of Tobit the father from blindness

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Haran: a city between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, lying northeast of Damascus at a distance of two hundred and eighty miles. It is a commercial city, and the meaning of its name is the road, since it lies on a trade route. Terah and his son Abraham sojourned in it before Abraham went to Canaan, and Jacob also lived in it twenty years, married in it and begot his sons.
Tobias and the angel reached Haran, which lies halfway on the road to Nineveh, on the eleventh day (see Map 2, p. 265).

It is noted on the map that Haran lies northwest of Nineveh, but it was a station on the road coming from Rages, and after it the traveler descends to the southeast to Nineveh. Tobias here is a type of those of the eleventh hour, who reached Tobit the father, that is, received salvation, and they are the Jews who were contemporaries of Christ and believed, though many had preceded them who died in the hope of the resurrection; he is also a type of the Gentiles far from the faith who believed in Christ.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Tobias wanted to hurry to see his parents to reassure them, and because the angel felt the parents' anxiety, he proposed to Tobias that he divide the caravan into two parts, that the two of them should hurry first (probably they rode a horse, or two), and the rest of the caravan would then follow them, which included Sara and the servants and maidservants (the household), whom he sometimes called the servants, and with them the cattle.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Tobias agreed, and then the angel reminded him to take with him a part of the gall of the fish, for he would need it.

Tobias's hurrying to reach his father is a type of Christ's ascension as the representative of all humanity, to prepare for His bride and His Church (Sara) a place, and to rejoice the heart of God the Father (Tobit the father). Tobias's escape from death and the salvation of Sara is a type of Christ's resurrection from the dead, offering redemption to His Church.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: In her longing to see her son, who was late in arriving, Anna used to go out every day and sit on the top of a hill outside Nineveh overlooking the roads leading to the city, for from there she could look a long distance. She did not tire of waiting, because of her love for her son. So the souls that love God await His coming, and as the Apostle Paul says: "having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ" (Phil 1:23).

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: One day, while she was watching the road, she saw from afar a person approaching, resembling her son in his movement, and with a mother's instinct she was certain that he was her son, so she hurried to give the good news to her husband Tobit.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Draw near: come close.

As they were approaching the house, the angel instructed Tobias what to do when he entered. He told him to offer worship and thanks to God, and then kiss his father. God is first in our life, in our afflictions and in our joy, and we ought to offer Him reverence with thanksgiving; these are the feelings of prayer, and after that, being filled with the grace of God and His love, we can express our love to our loved ones.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Anoint: from anointing, that is, smear.
Then he instructed him to put some of the gall of the fish on the eyes of Tobit the father, and his eyes would be opened and he would see everything and rejoice at seeing God.

The younger Tobias is a type of Christ and the gall a type of the sufferings He endured on the Cross for the salvation of humanity, while Tobit the father is a type of humanity, which received spiritual enlightenment in the sacrament of Baptism through the sufferings of Christ and His redemption, which the gall typifies.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Wagging its tail: moving its tail.

While they were speaking they came very near to the house, and the dog that had accompanied them on the journey ran ahead, wagging its tail, announcing its joy at returning to its home, and it was like a herald to Tobit and his wife of the arrival of the caravan at the house.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: When the dog reached the house and the mother saw it, she rejoiced and hurried to meet her son. Tobit the father, though blind, rose and ran too, forgetting his inability to see, and he kept stumbling on many things in his way, so one of the young men around him came forward to take his hand and help him to receive his son. The boy who took Tobit's hand is a type of John the Baptist, who prepared the way of Christ by his preaching and helped humanity, which was living in the darkness of sin and is typified by Tobit the father, to receive the good news of Christ, who is typified by the younger Tobias.

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: They went on: they remained and continued.

The meeting between Tobias and his parents was warm, and from the excess of their joy they wept. We note here that Tobias preceded his wife to his father's house, as Christ ascended to heaven to prepare a place for His Church, that she may be where He is (Jn 14:2).

entries.section: (1) The return of Tobias with the angel to his parents

paragraphs.text: Then all came forward to pray and bowed down in thanks to God, and afterward they sat and talked, and each expressed his feelings; and so they put God first before their personal talk, as we mentioned.

entries.section: (2) Sight returns to Tobit the father

paragraphs.text: Tobias told his father that he had with him a medicine to treat the eyes, which he had brought with him from the journey, and asked his permission to use this medicine on him, then he rose and smeared his father's eyes with the gall of the whale (the fish). The use of the gall of the whale for healing the illness of Tobit the father was an accepted thing at that time, since medicine among the ancient Egyptians was known and used the liver, the gall and fish to anoint the sick, so that they were healed of their illnesses.

Tobias believed the angel's word that his father would be healed, yet he obeyed and smeared his eyes with the gall of the whale, and this is what happens in the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick, when the priest anoints the sick person with oil and by faith he is healed of his illnesses; for the spirit believes and the body also shares when touched with a perceptible substance.

We note that the angel specified the substance suitable for healing the illness, namely the gall, and also specified who would smear the father's eyes with the substance, namely the younger Tobias, and this is a type of the specifying of the oil of the Anointing of the Sick for healing the sick, by the hand of the priest of the New Testament.

entries.section: (2) Sight returns to Tobit the father

paragraphs.text: Eggshell membrane: the thin membrane surrounding the white of a boiled egg beneath the dry shell.

Then their sitting continued in conversations of love, Tobias telling about his journey and what happened on it, and the parents telling about their circumstances. After about half an hour had passed, a thin membrane began to appear on the eyes of Tobit the father, so the younger Tobias took hold of the edge of this membrane and drew it from his father's eyes; his eyes were opened at once and he saw as he had before.

Although the healing was entirely from God by the work of His grace, we note that Tobias used a substance, the gall of the whale, and it may have been a membrane that he drew from his father's eyes. These material things were only to confirm the importance of spiritual striving in order to receive the work of divine grace. As the Lord Christ put clay on the eyes of the man born blind and asked him to wash, and as He asked those around Him to take away the stone from the door of the tomb of Lazarus (Jn 11:39), and likewise Saul of Tarsus, when he was baptized by the hand of Ananias the priest in Damascus, scales fell from his eyes and his eyes were opened (Acts 9:18). So the waiting of half an hour was to test the faith of Tobias the son and the father, for God sometimes delays His work, even for a short time, to test our faith, as takes place in the Holy Sacraments such as the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick, in which a prayer is offered for an hour and the sick person is signed with oil; besides the importance of prayer, it is an opportunity to test faith in the power of God who is able to heal.

We must complete our striving in order to receive divine grace from God who is able to do all things, and consequently our hearts should not be troubled, however hard the affliction is, or its solution seems impossible: "The things which are impossible with men are possible with God" (Lk 18:27).

entries.section: (2) Sight returns to Tobit the father

paragraphs.text: There was great joy at the miraculous healing of Tobit, in which all those around him and those who knew him shared.

At once the feelings of joy turned into glorification and thanksgiving to God, and this is the conduct of the children of God which drives them to praise every day in the Church, in thanksgiving to God for His salvation, which He accomplished on the Cross and offers to them in the Church and her sacraments.

entries.section: (2) Sight returns to Tobit the father

paragraphs.text: The beautiful thing is that there was not the slightest murmuring in Tobit the father, but he was accepting of the trial as a chastening from God, trusting in His mercy and the healing He had bestowed on him. Contentment and thanksgiving open the door to the work of God's grace with a person.

entries.section: (3) The safe arrival of Sara and the caravan

paragraphs.text: The younger Tobias went on telling his parents all the details of the journey and all the blessings of God which He had bestowed on him by means of Azarias, his companion and guide. The parents listened with joy and longing and thanked God for His blessings.

Azarias, that is, the angel Raphael, is a type, as we mentioned, of the Holy Spirit, and through him Tobias received the many benefits of God, for the Holy Spirit is the one who gives us the blessings of salvation which Christ accomplished on the Cross.

After seven days had passed, which went by quickly as if they were moments, from the excess of joy at Tobias's meeting with his parents, Sara arrived with the servants and maidservants and all the cattle and all the money, both what she took from her parents and what they obtained from Gabael. It represents God's blessings to His children who obey His commandments. The number seven is a type of the completeness of waiting for the blessing of God, and also points to the time of the Church's (Sara's) completing her striving on earth, until she reaches heaven.

If the younger Tobias is a type of Christ who arrived at His Father's house, that is, ascended to the heavens, then Sara, who is a type of the Church, arrived after him in heaven, where He had prepared a place for her, to be with Him forever, and with her all that she acquired in the world of virtues (typified by her material possessions of servants, money and cattle), and she acquired all this because of her union with Tobias, that is, Christ, who delivered her from the captivity of Satan (Asmodeus).

entries.section: (3) The safe arrival of Sara and the caravan

paragraphs.text: Ahior: a Hebrew name meaning other.
Nabat: a Hebrew name meaning God sees.

The relatives of Tobit the father came, when they heard the news of his healing and the return of his son married and with much money, to congratulate him. The two most famous names of his relatives mentioned by the Holy Bible are Ahior (other) and Nabat (God sees), and they point to the fact that if the affliction is prolonged, God the Almighty sees everything and finally pours out His mercies and rejoices the heart of His children.

entries.section: (3) The safe arrival of Sara and the caravan

paragraphs.text: All expressed their joy with a feast that lasted seven days. The feast is a type of the feast of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord, the source of our complete joy. The number seven is a type of the completeness of joy. And if Tobit the father is a type of the Father, his relatives point to the angels, who rejoice at the arrival of the Church in heaven, after the end of this world, and live in the heavenly feast forever. And if the Church, typified by Sara, rejoiced in the house of her father Raguel with a feast, this is a type of rejoicing in Christ on earth, but in heaven also there is another joy that cannot be expressed, typified by the feast held at Tobit the father's, who is a type of the Father.
Azarias reveals his identity

entries.section: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

paragraphs.text: After all these blessings had been received, Tobit the father took his son aside and began to discuss with him the wage that Azariah deserved, the man who had accompanied him on his journey.

entries.section: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

paragraphs.text: What should he give him in return for his abundant kindness to Tobias the son?

entries.section: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

paragraphs.text: So Tobias the son recalled the five great blessings that Azariah had done for him, which are:
1- He kept him safe and brought him back unharmed from this journey.
2- He recovered the money for him from Gabael.
3- He guided him to Sarah, married him to her, kept Satan away from them, and made her parents rejoice.
4- He rescued him from the fish (that is, the great fish) that was about to devour him.
5- He opened the eyes of Tobit the father.

From the foregoing, we see the father and his son appreciating the labor others had undertaken for them, and their gratitude, to the point that they call him holy and resolved to give him half of the possessions they had brought back from the journey.

entries.section: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

paragraphs.text: Their humility also appears in their saying: Will Azariah consent and accept half of the possessions?

If you are ready to sacrifice and give to God and to others in your time of distress, do not go back on your vows to God or on your promises to others, or on rewarding them for their labor when your problem is solved. Rather, be generous like Tobit and his son, appreciating the labor others have undertaken for you, and give generously, as God also gives to you generously.

entries.section: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

paragraphs.text: In humility, Tobit and his son took Azariah aside and begged him to accept half of what they had gained from this journey. We shall see that Azariah will take nothing from them and will make known to them who he is: the glorious archangel Raphael. From this we understand that God's gifts to us are free (Rom 3:24).

entries.section: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

paragraphs.text: The angel, however, spoke to them about something else: that they should glorify God and tell of His works with them.

entries.section: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

paragraphs.text: Rather, he made clear to them that, if the secrets of earthly kings ought to be kept hidden, for fear that harm may come to them if they are made known, since they are only men, then, on the contrary, the secrets of the King of kings and Lord of lords, and His work with men, ought to be proclaimed, so that all may bless God, especially in circumstances like those in which the people of God were living, exiled among the Gentiles, so that the children of God might be established in their faith and the Gentiles might see the work of God and believe. But this is on condition that a man does not abandon his humility, boasting when he recalls the works of God, or thinking himself better than others because of what has been done for him. The humility of Tobit and his son was evident, so there was no fear for them in proclaiming the works of God. The secret of the king signifies the mysteries of the Church, which only the faithful see and which are not spoken of or disclosed to unbelievers, for they will not understand them. In addition, the secret of the king is the personal relationship between the soul and God and its private experiences, which are not announced to people, as the Song of Songs says: "A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed" (Song 4:12). The general rule, then, is that personal experiences are not disclosed, and, when necessary, are attributed to someone unnamed, as the Apostle Paul spoke of a man he knew who was caught up to the third heaven, and he was speaking of himself. But in some cases, for the teaching of others, the teacher needs to declare the secrets of God, and this is done under spiritual guidance, as in the case of Tobit and his son, as the angel instructed them.

How beautiful it is for a person to proclaim the works of God while concealing himself, so that he is not fought by pride. So the Apostle Paul in the New Testament declared God's work with him, for God showed him the third heaven, that is, the paradise of bliss, but he hid himself, saying, "I knew a man" and did not say, "I saw" (2 Cor 12:2).

entries.section: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

paragraphs.text: After Azariah had called Tobit and his son to bless God and to proclaim His works, he showed them the importance of the three basic means of grace, which are prayer, fasting and almsgiving, and that they are better than all the treasures of the world, because through them a person is joined to God, the source of all spiritual and material wealth.

entries.section: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

paragraphs.text: Then he emphasized the importance of almsgiving, since it delivers a person from eternal death, forgives his sins, makes the mercies of God overflow upon him, and through it he inherits eternal life. For almsgiving is a person's going out of himself; then he feels for others and gives to them. This cannot happen except through a person's union with God, his love for Him, his repentance in humility, and his detachment from material things; then he is able to love others and to give himself for them.

entries.section: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

paragraphs.text: As for those who are preoccupied with their desires and their selfishness and do many evil things, by this conduct they harm themselves and head toward eternal perdition, through their separation from God, and so they become the worst enemies of themselves.

entries.section: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

paragraphs.text: Finally, Azariah began to disclose his secret and God's purpose in the life of Tobit, indeed God's purpose in all our lives.

entries.section: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

paragraphs.text: He showed how God cares about every act of worship we offer Him, especially fervent prayers that come from the heart, as well as the works of mercy we do, and the preferring of God's works to our own comfort and needs, even essential ones such as food and drink. Tobit did all of these, and the angel offered them up before God immediately, one after another. This shows God's concern for our love toward Him and that He values our works, even if they are small in the eyes of people, such as giving a cup of cold water, how much more if they are great works.

entries.section: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

paragraphs.text: And after Tobit's sonship to God and his love for Him had been made evident, God wished to prove him, so that he might have a better place in heaven. So He allowed him the trial of blindness and poverty, and before that, the king's pursuit of him and his attempt to kill him. Yet Tobit stood firm in his faith and in his love for God.
Likewise Sarah also stood firm in her faith in God, despite the failure of her seven marriages.

entries.section: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

paragraphs.text: And finally the angel declared that God had sent him to heal Tobit the father of his blindness, and Sarah, his son's wife (his daughter-in-law), of Satan's assault on any man who tried to marry her.

Thus it is shown that God, the Almighty, watches all our works with care and allows trial only for our good, and only for a time. Then He removes it from us and blesses us with more abundant blessings.

entries.section: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

paragraphs.text: And finally Azariah revealed his true identity, which is that he is the archangel Raphael, one of the seven archangels who stand before God.

entries.section: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

paragraphs.text: At this heavenly declaration they fell on their faces to the ground, trembling with great fear, when they realized that they were in the presence of the great archangel Raphael. This shows their humility and the fear of God that was in their hearts.

entries.section: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

paragraphs.text: So the angel reassured them and gave them peace, and explained to them that his appearing, his accompanying Tobias the son, and everything he had done with them were by God's providence and will.

entries.section: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

paragraphs.text: Then he explained to them that his human conduct in eating and drinking and all the material things he had done was merely an outward appearance, but in truth he has no need of these foods or of anything material, since his spiritual food is the love of God and prayer. And let us know that the stronger and higher being (the spiritual) can easily resemble the lesser creature (the material) in eating, drinking, walking, sleeping, and so on; on the contrary, a material creature, such as a human being or an animal, cannot resemble spiritual creatures, that is, the angels. Yet a human being, since he is a spiritual and material creature, can share with the angels in some works, such as prayer, love and self-giving.

entries.section: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

paragraphs.text: Then the glorious archangel Raphael bade them farewell and stressed two things: blessing and glorifying the Lord, and then speaking of God's works to others, so that they may believe and be established in their faith.

entries.section: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

paragraphs.text: After the angel ascended to heaven and disappeared from sight, Tobit and his son remained prostrate before God, in reverence, offering prayers of thanksgiving and blessing God for three hours, with feelings of fear and joy mingled together within them. Then they rose in joy and began to tell all their relatives and loved ones of the greatness of God with them.

Thus we see that beholding heavenly things is something very great, which required the father and his son to remain prostrate before God for three hours, and the number three points to the fullness of reverence. How much more, then, should our feeling be when we approach the Holy Sacraments, such as the sacrament of confession and the sacrament of Holy Communion? In the story of Tobit we find the clearest appearance of the glorious archangel Raphael in the Holy Bible, and the Fathers interpret other appearances in the Holy Bible as being of the angel Raphael, and they are:-

1- The appearance of an angel to Christ to strengthen Him in the Garden of Gethsemane (Lk 22:39-43), for the angel Raphael is the angel of help. Thus the angel Raphael served Christ, to whom Tobit points as a type, just as he served Tobit, who is a symbol of Christ.
2- The appearance of an angel who stirred the water in the pool of Bethesda (Jn 5:1-4). The angel Raphael is also called the angel of healing.
The closing prayer of Tobit the father

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: After glorifying God, who is glorified forever, he declared that it is part of God's mercy that He allows affliction and then returns and has mercy on us.

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: And if He allows a wound, He returns and heals it, and if a person feels that he has gone down to the depths, God returns and lifts him up, has mercy on him and honors him. This gives hope to everyone in affliction: let him be assured that it will pass and that God's tender hand will have mercy on him, and a person feels the fatherhood of God, who does not allow our affliction to the end, but only for a time. Therefore, when King David sinned by numbering the people and becoming proud, and deserved punishment, and God asked him to choose a punishment, he said, let me fall into the hand of God and not into the hand of men, trusting in the mercy of God, who returns and removes his affliction from him (2 Sam 24:14). By this verse God removes from minds the pagan idea that proclaims a god of good and a god of evil; He is the one God, the Almighty, who gives good things and allows evils, for everything is in His hand alone, and He has affirmed this meaning in other places of the Holy Bible, such as (Isa 40:7; 1 Sam 2:6-8).

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: Then one of God's purposes in the affliction of His people is shown, in allowing them to go into captivity: that they might proclaim God among the Gentiles, by their pure lives and good conduct, their confession of God and their speaking of His works, so that the Gentiles might believe in God.
And this is a clear declaration that God offers His salvation to the whole world and not only to the Jews.

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: He also declares that the cause of the affliction is the sins of the people, but God, in His love, has mercy on them and removes the affliction from them when they repent.

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: Then he calls to his people, after they have seen God's work with him, to glorify God and confess His holiness in continual prayers and constant thanksgiving, and by this their conduct becomes upright and glorifies God. This means that whoever prays much from his heart has his life purified and walks uprightly according to the will of God.

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: Then Tobit continues his prayer by praising God and glorifying Him, because He has mercy on His people who sinned against Him, and this shows the extent of His mercy. The importance of this praise is that it takes place in captivity, that is, Tobit praises God while still in affliction, a captive who has not yet returned to his homeland. How beautiful it is to praise God at all times, even in times of distress.

God also shows the Gentiles the greatness of His people and His hatred of sin, such that He disciplines His beloved people who believe in Him; by this He calls the Gentiles to believe in Him and to turn away from the sin that angers Him, and if they do not repent, He will discipline them and take vengeance on them.

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: Then Tobit calls all sinners to return to God with a pure life, confident of His mercy toward them, for He "will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4).

entries.section: (1) Thanking God and blessing Him

paragraphs.text: Then he calls all the children of God to join with his own rejoicing soul in praising and glorifying God, and even to set aside whole days for praise and joy.
Praise God first, and your heart will be filled with joy, and then you will be able to call others to praise.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Here in his prayer Tobit addresses Jerusalem, the great city in which is the temple of God. It also signifies the human soul and signifies the Church. So he says to Jerusalem, or to his own soul, that because of the multitude of sin God condemned it and allowed it affliction and captivity.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: But with steadfast hope he says to her, give thanks to God and bless Him. And how can a person bless God while in affliction, unless he is confident of God's mercy, and his hope in Him is steadfast, certain that He will remove this affliction from him? Therefore he says to Jerusalem that the ruined temple in her will be built again, her captive children will return to her, and she will rejoice forever.

This is what happens with the repentant human soul, which feels that the affliction is because of its sins, thanks God for everything, and trusts that God will return and build His dwelling within it, reign over it, fill its heart, and bring back to it all its captive children, that is, its senses, thoughts and all its members, returning pure, as members of Christ, and it lives a life of joy and constant praise.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: "You will shine with a glad radiance": you will glow with a joyful light.
"They will regard": they will consider.

Then he promises Jerusalem that she will be exalted above all the nations and will shine with greatness, joy and splendor that dazzle the eyes, so that all peoples will bow before her in reverence, worshiping in esteem and respect; indeed, the nations will bring her gifts and will feel that she is a holy land in which God dwells.
And history bears witness to this, for Alexander the Great, when he reached Jerusalem, felt the greatness of the temple, bowed down before it and offered his sacrifices.
And these words are a prophecy of the Gentiles' faith in Christianity and their worship in the new Jerusalem, that is, the Church, which believers from all the peoples of the world enter.

And this is what happens with the soul over which God reigns: He glorifies it among men on earth, and also in heaven, and gives it awe in the eyes of all, so that they seek its good pleasure, since they feel that God dwells in it.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And for the glorifying of the great name of God in you, O Jerusalem, whoever despises and scorns you, the curse of God comes upon him, but he who honors you and builds you up, God blesses.

Thus, when God dwells in a person and is glorified in his works, all the wicked who persecute him are cursed by God, that is, the punishment of God comes upon them, even if after a while, and then their punishment is completed in eternal torment. But he who honors the spiritual person and works for his edification, God blesses.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Then he continues his prayer, calling Jerusalem to rejoice in her children gathered in her around the Lord, and the Lord blesses her.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Then he pronounces blessed those who love Jerusalem and seek her good and peace.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And he calls himself among the lovers of Jerusalem, to bless the Lord for His mercy and for the deliverance of Jerusalem from destruction.

So also the human soul rejoices in the gathering of all its members and senses around the Lord, and exults in worshiping Him, praising Him and working for His good pleasure. Likewise the Lord blesses those who fear Him and all who love them, and all the lovers of the Lord thank Him for His love and mercy toward His children. The Church also rejoices in the gathering of her children in her, praising God. And everyone who loves the Church and seeks her peace, the Lord blesses, and all the lovers of the Church glorify God for His works and His mercy to His Church.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And finally, he closes his prayer with prophecies about the coming glory of Jerusalem, and pronounces himself blessed if any of his descendants remain to see this glory. Here he prophesies about the glory of Jerusalem in her return from captivity, and also about the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption of His Church, and in the end he prophesies about the heavenly Jerusalem, so we find a clear similarity between his prophecies and the words of the Revelation of John the Theologian in the New Testament.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: He prophesies about the gates of Jerusalem, that is, her entrances. They are of sapphire, whose color is blue, the color of heaven, meaning that those who enter her will have the thought and the pure spiritual life of heaven. It is also a hard stone, which signifies spiritual firmness, strength and patience, and it is purified by fire, because the children of the Kingdom bear the cross and endure many sufferings, and so are crowned in heaven.

The gates are also of emerald. Its color is green, and it signifies freshness and vitality, meaning that those who enter her through their spiritual striving and the work of the Holy Spirit in them grow in the knowledge of God and live with Him forever. After that he speaks about the walls of the city. The walls are what surround the city, fortify it and keep every harm from it, and they are made of precious stones, that is, of the most precious thing, for nothing is more precious than the name of the Lord and the blood of Christ the Redeemer, who saves us from death and by whom we take refuge from all the wars of the devil, as the Holy Bible says, "The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: He continues his prophecies about Jerusalem, or about the human soul that lives with God, or about the Church, and describes her streets as paved with pure white stone. The streets are the place where people gather, so he declares that the gathering of her children is marked by purity, and their dealings by uprightness and splendor (white). And the stone points to strength and firmness, meaning that her children enjoy spiritual firmness and a strong life with God, so they are not shaken by the changes of life, but live in steadfast faith.

And in the streets of the city (that is, the roads that connect her various parts) they sing Hallelujah, which signifies that the praise of the name of the Lord is what binds the children of this city to one another.

entries.section: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: And at the end he blesses God, who glorified Jerusalem, or His Church, or the souls that love Him, and even exalted her above the whole world, by His reigning over her forever, so that He gives her joy in His fellowship and His love. The end of Tobit's life and his final testament

entries.section: (1) The death of Tobit in a good old age

paragraphs.text: In the last chapter the book summarizes for us the life of St. Tobit the father, who lived fifty-six years in a godly life with God and in good works. Then he was struck with blindness and remained four years in this severe affliction, and at its end his son traveled with the angel Raphael, then returned, married to Sarah, and opened his father's eyes. Tobit was sixty years old when he saw again. Then he lived joyfully with God, with his wife, his son and all his loved ones, and even with his grandchildren, in the fear of God, until he died in a good old age, forty-two years after his sight returned, so that he was then one hundred and two years old, and that was around the year 631 BC. He was buried in the city of Nineveh, honored with great honor by his sons and all his loved ones.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: Before the death of Tobit the father, he summoned his son Tobias, who had begotten seven sons, and gave them all his last testament, which is full of joyful prophecies for the people of God. And Sarah, who signifies the Church by her marriage to Tobias the son, who signifies Christ, bore seven sons, who signify the seven sacraments of the Church, which Christ gave to His Church.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: Then he confirmed the words of the prophets, such as Nahum (Nah 3:1), that Nineveh would be utterly destroyed. This was something very strange, because it was the greatest city in the world, being the capital of the Assyrian Empire that ruled the world.

This shows the vanity of perishable material powers, so the children of God should not depend on them. Likewise, let no one be deceived by his strength and authority, but let him look to God, the only power that is steadfast in this life and forever, so that he is not troubled by afflictions, or by the threats of others and their domination, but takes refuge in God in everything, even before thinking of his own strength or the strength of those around him. Thus his heart is at peace, in God's hands, under all circumstances.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: He also proclaimed the return of the people of God from captivity to Jerusalem. For after the Assyrian captivity, in which Tobit was living, the Babylonian captivity would come, and after it the kingdom of the Medes and Persians would arise, at the beginning of which the Jews would return to Jerusalem. He also proclaimed that the city and all Judea would be filled with those who fear God and love to worship Him, for the ruined house of God would be built again, and they would offer in it their sacrifices and their worship to the one God.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: He even prophesied about the faith of the Gentiles and their rulers, who would exalt Jerusalem, bow down to God in it, worship Him and join His people, leaving the worship of idols.

This was not a prophecy only about Jerusalem and the return from captivity, but also about the world's return to the faith and the spread of Christianity everywhere, before the Second Coming of Christ.
The Gentiles' return to God would take place through their faith in Christ, as many from the different nations of the world believed.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: Then Tobit the father continues his last testament, calling his sons to true worship of God from the heart and to care for pleasing Him in all their lives.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: He also charged them to teach their children to walk uprightly, and to observe justice in all their dealings, so that they would wrong no one. Then he stressed the importance of almsgiving and mercy. And finally, to take care to remember the name of the Lord at all times, to praise Him and to glorify Him, in order to remain in His company and constant fellowship.

entries.section: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

paragraphs.text: Then he closed his testament with a specific command, which was to leave the city of Nineveh as soon as his wife Anna died and was buried with him in one tomb, so that they might escape destruction in Nineveh, the great city, which would be destroyed as a result of its many evils.
Nineveh signifies the world, which will perish by its iniquity, and therefore the children of God must go out from it, that is, be strangers to its desires and its sins and live for Christ.

entries.section: (3) Tobias goes to his parents-in-law

paragraphs.text: "Closed their eyes": what those close to the dead do immediately after their death, that is, he was present at their death and burial.
"Obtained": received and gained.

Tobias the son took care to carry out his father's testament. A few years after his father was buried, his mother died, and he buried her with honor beside his father. Then he set out with all his sons and grandchildren, taking all his money, and traveled to his parents-in-law, Raguel and Anna, who rejoiced greatly at meeting him and their daughter, and all their children whom they had longed to see. Raguel and Anna had by then become old.

Thus the faith of Tobias the son and his obedience to his father are shown, for he abandoned the great city of Nineveh, with all its glory, confident of the truth of his father's word that it would be destroyed.
May we obey the commandments of God, however much they conflict with our human wisdom and the thoughts of the world.

entries.section: (3) Tobias goes to his parents-in-law

paragraphs.text: After God had bestowed many blessings on Tobit the father and the son, He also bestowed them on the righteous Raguel and Anna, for they lived years with the children of their daughter Sarah, and completed their lives in godliness and prayer, rejoicing in the Lord, until they died in a good old age, and Tobias buried them with great honor.

Here we see the joy that distinguishes the children of God from the people of the world, this joy that continues throughout their lives, even in the midst of afflictions and in old age, when a person grows weak and the battles of fear, anxiety and complaining increase. But the grace of God preserves their joy for them until the end of their life on earth, so that afterward they may speak with Him in heaven in eternal joy.

entries.section: (3) Tobias goes to his parents-in-law

paragraphs.text: And Tobias the son lived many days in goodness and righteousness. He saw his grandchildren to the fifth generation, until he died at the age of ninety-nine.

entries.section: (3) Tobias goes to his parents-in-law

paragraphs.text: His sons, relatives and loved ones continued to live a good life, as a good example in the midst of the world, declaring the name of God.
For one of God's blessings on a person is to live many days on earth in the fear of God, and not only that, but also to have righteous offspring who bear witness to God.
And so this great book ends with abundant blessings and lasting joy for the righteous children of God, who endured many afflictions and held fast to their faith.
A- The prayer of Tobit when he was in affliction (ch. 3:1-6). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:
1- Submission to God's ordering of events.
2- Confession of sins and repentance.
3- Asking for God's mercy.
4- Acknowledging deserving punishment.
5- Reliance on God.
6- Suffering that borders on death.
B- The prayer of Sarah when she was in affliction (ch. 3, 13:22). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:
1- Waiting for God's mercy.
2- God's forgiveness in affliction.
3- Clinging to God.
4- Asking for the removal of the affliction.
5- Suffering to the point of death.
6- Perplexity over the cause of the affliction, because she:
a- She walked in.
b- Sought marriage in the purity of God.
7- Acceptance of God's will.
8- The loftiness of God's wisdom.
9- The blessings of affliction and its crowns.
10- God rescues His children from afflictions.
11- Faith in God's saving power.
12- Glorifying God.
C- The prayer of Tobit after his healing (ch. 13). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:-
1- Glorifying God in word and in deed.
2- God's allowing affliction and giving blessings from it.
3- The responsibility of the children of God to make Him known to the world.
4- Affliction is discipline for our sins.
5- Deliverance from afflictions through God's mercy.
6- A call to repentance and to glorify God.
7- Prophecy of the return from captivity and the glory of Jerusalem, whether through Christ the Savior or in the Kingdom of Heaven.
D- A comparison between the prayers of Tobit and Sarah when they were in affliction:
There is a great similarity between the two prayers in the following:
1- Asking for God's mercy.
2- Surrender to God's will.
3- Confession of sins and repentance.
4- Suffering to the point of death.
5- Glorifying God and blessing His judgments.
E- A comparison between the two prayers of Tobit, when he was in affliction and after his healing from it:- There is a similarity between the two prayers in the following:-
1- Glorifying God.
2- Sin is the cause of affliction.
3- A call to repentance.

But there is a clear difference between them, which is that the first prayer is marked by the suffering of pain and the expectation of death, while the second prayer is marked by thanksgiving, praise, faith in salvation, and a call to the children of God to glorify Him and to enjoy the splendor of Jerusalem.
