1- The marriage procedures, which consisted of Raguel, the bride's father, writing the marriage contract, taking his daughter's hand and handing her over to her bridegroom; here he represents the priest of the family (ch. 7:15).
2- The continence of Tobias and Sarah for three days and their prayers (ch. 8:4).
3- Holding the wedding feast in the fear of God (ch. 9:12).
4- The instructions of Sarah's parents to her, with their five contents (ch. 10:13). A summary of the most important characteristics of the angel Raphael
1- He is one of the seven archangels who stand before God at all times (Tob 12:15).
2- He appeared as a guide for the roads of the cities under the name Azariah, in the form of a young man of handsome appearance (Tob 5:5, 6, 18).
3- After showing his readiness to guide Tobias the son to Rages (Tob 5:14, 20), he met Tobit the father to reassure him that he would bring his son there.
4- When the fish attacked Tobias the son, he saved him from it and charged him to take its heart, liver and gall and to salt the rest of its flesh (Tob 6:3, 5).

5- He guided Tobias the son to marry Sarah (Tob 6:12). He reassured Raguel her father and advised Tobias to burn the liver and the heart when he entered the marriage chamber and to abstain from Sarah for three days (Tob 6:
6- During the marriage celebration he went to Gabael in Rages, recovered the loan from him and took him with him, to meet Tobias the son and congratulate him on his marriage (Tob 9).
7- He accompanied Tobias the son on the road back to his father and mother, then divided the procession into two parts, and he and Tobias went ahead to meet his parents and reassure them (Tob 11).

8- When Tobit and his son tried to offer him money, he thanked them and declared to them who he was, that he is the archangel Raphael and that he had been offering up the prayers of Tobit the father and Sarah. The father and his son bowed down before him, and he ascended to heaven (Tob 12). Tobit the father
1- Tobit was a young man of the tribe of Naphtali, who lived in Upper Galilee and was taken captive to the city of Nineveh (Tob 1:1, 3).
2- He was married to a woman of his tribe named Anna, and had by her one son, whom he named after himself (Tob 1:9).

3- He was a righteous man; even as a young man he was diligent in going to the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem to worship and to offer the firstfruits and the tithes, and he did not go to the golden calves that Jeroboam had made (Tob 1:5-7).
4- After his captivity in Nineveh he did not eat of the food of the Gentiles as the rest of the Jews did (Tob 1:12).

5- God gave him favor in the eyes of King Shalmaneser, and he found grace with him, as he worked as purveyor of supplies in the king's palace (Tob 1:13). He used the nature of his work, with its travel throughout the land, to visit his brethren in captivity and remind them of God's commandments (Tob 1:14), and he would help the needy among them, as when he lent ten talents of silver to Gabael, who was in the city of Rages, and took a bond from him for it (ch. 1:16, 17).
6- He took care to bury the dead of the Jews whom the king killed, who persecuted the Jews with great zeal (Tob 1:20), (Tob 2:3, 4), regardless of the reproach of his relatives (Tob 2:8).

7- When King Sennacherib learned of what Tobit was doing in burying the dead, he wanted to kill him, so Tobit fled with his wife and his son, leaving all his money. But God delivered him, for after forty-five days the king's two sons killed him, and Tobit returned to his house and recovered his money (Tob 1:23-25).

8- On one occasion, after burying one of the dead, he returned to his house exhausted and slept beside his house, and the droppings of a bird fell into his eyes and took away his sight (Tob 2:11). He was fifty-six years old (Tob 14:3), and he did not complain despite the reproaches of his wife and his relatives (Tob 2:15-17).

9- His wife was compelled to work at weaving to support the family, after life had become hard for them. Yet, upon hearing the sound of a kid in the house, he feared it might be stolen and warned his wife, who kept reproaching him for his care for God's law, his almsgiving and his hope in God (Tob 2:19-22).

10- When Tobit's need became severe, he summoned his son and informed him of the loan that was with Gabael and asked him to recover it (Tob 4:22). He told him that he had a bond for the money and asked him to take a guide who would show him the way and to give him his wage (Tob 5:3, 4). The son found a young man named Azariah and brought him in to his father, who blessed him, and he set out with his son to travel and recover the loan (Tob 25).
11- He was a man of prayer, who took refuge in God in every matter (Tob 3:1-6, 13).
12- He was a successful father of a family, and he taught his son the commandments of God when he thought he was near death (ch. 4).

13- His hope in God never ceased, and he was certain of His protection of his son Tobias, even when he was late past the time of his return, and he would comfort his wife, assuring her that he would return (Tob 10:6).

14- His son returned after his marriage and the recovery of the loan and anointed his father's eyes with the gall of the fish, and his sight returned to him; he was then sixty years old (Tob 11:13-15).

15- Tobit tried to reward Azariah (the angel Raphael) by giving him half of what his son had brought (Tob 12:5); then Azariah told him the truth of who he was, that he was the angel of the Lord, and he and his son bowed down on the ground and blessed God (Tob 12:11-22).

16- After he regained his sight he lived forty-two years and saw his grandchildren, and he died at the age of one hundred and two and was buried with honor in Nineveh (Tob 14:1, 2), after instructing his son to bury his mother and then leave Nineveh, because it would be destroyed (Tob 14:12). Then he uttered prophecies about the return from captivity, the destruction of Nineveh and the heavenly Jerusalem (Tob 13). Tobias the son
1- He is the only son of Tobit and Anna, who were of the tribe of Naphtali, and he was born in Galilee and was named after his father (Tob 1:1, 9).

2- He helped his father in doing good and in burying the dead; he would tell his father if he saw one of the dead of the children of Israel, and he would invite the godly to his father's feasts (Tob 2:2, 3).

3- He was marked by complete obedience, to the point that he agreed to go and recover the debt without knowing how to do it, and answered his father, "All that you have commanded me I will do" (Tob 5:1); therefore he deserved to be accompanied by an angel.

4- When he went out to look for a guide, the angel of God Raphael met him in the person of Azariah and told him that he had stayed with Gabael in the city of Rages (Tob 5:8), and he went in with Tobias the son to the father and reassured him that he would accompany the son to Gabael and bring the young man back safe (Tob 5:15, 20).
5- Tobias made preparations for the journey and bade his parents farewell; he traveled with his dog, in the company of Azariah, and they reached the river Tigris and spent the night there.

6- When Tobias the son went in to wash in the river, a great fish (a whale) attacked him, and he cried out to Azariah, who commanded him to pull the fish by its gills onto the land. It yielded to him, and he took from it its heart, liver and gall, as the angel commanded him, for uses that would appear later (Tob 16:1-5).

7- Azariah (the angel) guided him to go to Raguel his kinsman and to marry his daughter Sarah, and reassured him that what had befallen her former husbands, who died, would not befall him (Tob 6:11-17).
8- He married Sarah, and when they entered the chamber they burned the fish's liver, and the angel Raphael drove the devil Asmodeus far away from him.
9- Tobias and Sarah kept praying for three nights, and then, after the third night had passed, he was joined to her (Tob 8:

10- Tobias asked the angel to go to Gabael, collect the debt and invite him to his wedding, so that he would not be slow in returning to his father; for he had to remain two weeks in the wedding celebrations, as his father-in-law Raguel requested of him (Tob 8:23; Tob 9:1-5).

11- Tobias loved his parents, so he could not grant Raguel's request that he remain with him more than the two weeks, and he knew how anxious they were. So he took his wife and half of Raguel's possessions, which he gave him, of servants, cattle and maidservants, and traveled back to his parents (Tob 10:8-10).
12- When he reached Haran, which is midway on the road to Nineveh, he left his wife and the caravan in order to hasten to meet his parents (Tob 11:1-3).
13- When he met his father he took out the gall of the fish and anointed his eyes with it, as the angel had charged him, and the father regained his sight (Tob 11:13).
14- He asked his father to reward Azariah (the angel) for all that he had done, and then the angel declared to them who he was, and they bowed down before him (Tob 12:15-22).

15- God granted him seven sons. He buried his father in Nineveh as he had charged him. And after his mother died and was buried beside his father, he took his wife and his sons and left Nineveh, according to his father's testament, and went to his parents-in-law.

16- God blessed him and he saw his sons' sons to the fifth generation, and he buried his parents-in-law and took all their possessions, then died in the fear of the Lord, having completed ninety-nine years (Tob 14:5, 14-16). Sarah
1- She is Sarah the daughter of Raguel and Anna, who lived in the city of Rages in Media (Tob 3:7).
2- She had been married to seven men, one after another. A devil named Asmodeus would kill her husbands when they went in to her (Tob 3:8).
3- She suffered from the reproaches of her maidservant, and she offered fervent prayers and many fasts to God (Tob 3:9-25).

4- Tobias the son came forward to marry her, according to the counsel of Azariah (the angel). And Raguel agreed, despite his fear that what had befallen her previous husbands would befall Tobias (Tob 7:10-13).

5- She and Tobias remained in prayer for three nights, that God might bless them, and after that they were joined in holy marriage, after Tobias had burned the fish's liver, and the angel seized the devil who had been causing the death of her previous husbands (Tob 8:2-7).

6- She left her father's house with her husband Tobias, after the wedding feast, which lasted two weeks (Tob 8:23). Her father gave her half of his possessions, of servants and cattle, and her parents charged her to honor her parents-in-law, love her husband and care for her household (Tob 10:10-13).
7- She reached her parents-in-law a week after her husband's arrival, and they received her with joy and made her a feast for seven days.
8- She bore seven sons, and after sharing with her husband in burying her parents-in-law she left Nineveh.
9- She went with her husband to her parents and lived with them until their death, and she saw her grandchildren.
Symbols of Christ and the Church. Tobit signifies Christ. Tobias the son signifies Christ in the following:
1- Tobias had his father's name, just as Christ has the name of His Father, being called Emmanuel, that is, God with us.
2- He did the same works as his father, which are works of mercy and burying the dead, and Christ went about everywhere doing good, like His Father, the Giver of good things.
3- He traveled with the angel serving him and bringing him to his bride Sarah, and Christ became incarnate and the angels serve Him, to redeem His bride, the Church.

4- Satan attacked him in the form of the fish and in the form of the devil Asmodeus, at his marriage, and Tobias triumphed over him. And Christ triumphed over Satan, in the temptation on the mountain and on the cross, when He bound him.

5- He married Sarah, who was tormented and found no rest with the seven husbands who were killed. And Christ married the Church, which did not find its salvation by all the ways in the Old Testament, but obtained salvation through Christ in the New Testament.

6- Raguel dug a grave for Tobias, because he believed he was among the dead, but the maidservant found him alive with his bride and gave Raguel and his wife the good news that they were alive. And Christ entered the tomb but rose, and Magdalene announced His resurrection.

7- Tobias was joined to Sarah and remained with her three days in prayer and continence, then was united with her, to beget sons on the third day. And Christ was joined to His Church and bore her sins on the cross, and on the third day rose from the dead, to give her new life and to beget from her many sons by faith, who are the sons of the New Testament.
8- Tobias recovered the debt from Gabael and gave him back the bond. And Christ paid the debt that was against us by His blood on the cross and offered us salvation.

9- Tobias's parents-in-law tried to keep him with them longer, with his bride, in their house, but he insisted on returning to his father. And Christ ascended to His Father despite His disciples' attachment to Him.

10- Tobias reached his father with the angel and gave him the news of his marriage, and after seven days Sarah arrived. And Christ ascended to heaven with the angels, to prepare a place for His Church, that is, His faithful children, whom He received after Him in Paradise.
11- Tobias healed his father's eyes by placing his hand with the gall upon them. And Christ healed the sick by touching them, such as putting clay on the eyes of the man born blind, and he saw.
